Title: Meta faces 'tobacco moment' in landmark child harm trial
Article:
OAKLAND: Jury selection kicked off on Wednesday in a California courtroom where Instagram and Facebook owner Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial which experts describe as social media's big tobacco moment.
Federal Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers and lawyers for both sides probed prospective jurors about their views of social media and Meta, asking if they personally had social media accounts, whether their kids use social media, and if they think social media is responsible for mental health, among other questions.
Some said they believed that social media plays a role in mental health, with one person comparing the serotonin boost that some people feel from "doomscrolling" to using cocaine.
Eight people were picked Wednesday afternoon to serve on the jury. They will play an advisory role in the trial, with the judge making the final decision.
A coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps and violating state laws.
Four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.
Top prosecutors from those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.
Meta "strongly disagrees with these allegations" and is "confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people," a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has "listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement."
Although it's not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.
"It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s," Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley's Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.
While such cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, similar to when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.
- 'PROTECTING TEENS'  -
By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.
Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with advertisements featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as "Joe Camel."
Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach US$1 billion.
In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta's apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as US$1.4 trillion, close to Meta's entire market value, which hovers around US$1.5 trillion.
Despite the eye-popping number, money isn't Meta's biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.
"The huge issue here is reputational harm" and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.
"Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning," as well, he said.
Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.
The case could be "the beginning of a broader reckoning" for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.
It will be important to see the "gap" between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.
Meta is "confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts," the company told AFP last week.
In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for US$27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.
On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.--AFP

Title: Malaysia's multi-billion BESS race
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Renewable energy (RE) construction flows in Malaysia are expected to pick up in the coming months, with battery energy storage systems (BESS) being the next phase of growth.
Malaysia is mandating BESS for major solar power projects nationwide to ensure grid stability. The country aims to raise RE to 70 per cent of installed power generation capacity by 2050, a target that will require a significant increase in energy storage to manage fluctuations in generation.
The government has started procuring it. In November 2024, the Energy Commission opened Malaysia's first competitive bidding process for utility-scale BESS, offering 400 MW/1,600 MWh across four projects. Each project is 100 MW/400 MWh and was targeted for commercial operation from this year.
Market insiders said that is a significant signal because it establishes BESS as part of Malaysia's electricity infrastructure rather than merely a private-sector add-on.
Malaysia has emerged as a major Southeast Asian data centre hub, attracting billions of ringgit in investments as global technology firms expand their digital infrastructure, leading to higher demand for reliable, round-the-clock electricity.
Data centres consume huge amounts of electricity and, critically, cannot tolerate prolonged interruptions. Traditionally, critical facilities have relied heavily on diesel generators for backup, said an insider, adding that BESS provides another option.
"A data centre could combine grid plus solar plus BESS plus conventional backup. The battery can respond almost instantaneously when the grid fails or fluctuates, while also potentially being used for other purposes when there is no outage," the insider said.
A July 2026 Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) report described battery storage as the next phase of growth for Malaysia's RE construction sector and referred to the opportunity as a billion ringgit.
HLIB said major RE programmes, including the large-scale solar 6 (LSS6) and corporate renewable energy supply scheme (CRESS), are expected to require storage capabilities, prompting developers to bring forward battery procurement plans in the second half of 2026.
PUC Bets on Multibillion-Ringgit BESS Boom
PUC Bhd is betting on a potential multibillion-ringgit BESS market in Malaysia, as the country ramps up solar deployment and grapples with rising power demand from data centres and other energy-intensive industries.
The digital services company is seeking to enter the sector through the proposed RM6.75 million acquisition of H BESS Sdn Bhd, giving PUC exposure to a fast-growing segment of the RE value chain.
PUC managing director Cheong Chia Chou said H BESS was a suitable strategic fit, as it provides PUC with an existing operating platform, allowing the company to enter the sector without having to build capabilities from the ground up.
He also said the timing was favourable as energy storage was shifting from a supporting technology to a critical component of the power system.
H BESS is involved in the assembly and supply of BESS solutions and has secured a letter of intent for a 4,626 kilowatt-hour BESS project at a five-star hotel in Kuala Lumpur.
The company has a partnership with China-based battery storage manufacturer Hithium Tech HK to establish a BESS assembly line in Malaysia.
Cheong said the proposed facility could support local manufacturing capabilities, with a targeted production capacity of up to 2.0 gigawatt-hours (GWh) annually if completed.
"For PUC, this creates the potential to grow the business with strong internal and external technology support, as well as local production capabilities.
Yong Tzen Wae, director of H BESS Sdn Bhd, said, "We will start by importing and installing systems, then gradually localise assembly and build up our capabilities in Malaysia."
"We see potential to become a regional player because every country will eventually require some level of localisation for energy storage solutions."
Lithium is among the major global battery storage manufacturers, while lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, technology has gained wider adoption because of its safety, durability and cost competitiveness.
"The technology is proven. It is already widely used globally and is now expanding into Southeast Asia," Yong added.
The proposed H BESS acquisition will be funded through a private placement of as many as 304.8 million new PUC shares, equivalent to 10 per cent of the company's existing issued share capital.
At an indicative issue price of 3.44 sen a share, the placement is expected to raise about RM10.49 million. Of the proceeds, RM6.75 million will be used to fund the acquisition, RM3.02 million for working capital and RM720,000 for related expenses.
The acquisition of H BESS is expected to create a new recurring growth avenue for PUC, Cheong said, adding that the deal includes a profit guarantee of RM3.5 million in aggregate audited net profit over financial years 2026 to 2028.
This provides additional earnings protection during the expansion phase, he said.
"We believe the timing is right. Things are just beginning. The key is to accelerate and capture market share. We see BESS as a new growth pillar that complements our existing businesses," Cheong said.
RE Growth Makes BESS Inevitable
Malaysia's electricity grid currently has about 2.0 per cent RE penetration, and a higher share would require greater storage capacity to maintain grid stability, said Datuk Chua Sai Men, director of H BESS Sdn Bhd.
Once RE reaches a certain threshold, the requirement for BESS becomes unavoidable, he said.
He said demand for BESS solutions is expected to rise alongside the growth of renewable energy adoption, supported by government-led initiatives such as the LSS6 programme.
The LSS6 programme, which includes a requirement for 1,250MW of BESS capacity, would provide further support for the development of the sector, Chua said.
"With favourable policies and increasing market demand, we believe PUC is well positioned to capture long-term opportunities in the energy storage sector," he said.
Chua said the opportunity extended beyond utility-scale projects to commercial and industrial (C&I) users, particularly as electricity demand rises from data centres.
Data centres require large amounts of reliable power, while solar can provide an additional source of electricity. Batteries could therefore play a key role in managing the intermittency of solar generation and ensuring a more stable power supply.
The economics of BESS could also improve as electricity tariffs rise, potentially making energy storage more attractive to commercial and industrial customers seeking to optimise power consumption and reduce exposure to peak electricity costs.
"Once you put in solar, you need batteries. Data centres cannot depend on intermittent power supply," he said.
BESS could also increasingly compete with conventional diesel backup systems used by critical facilities, offering a lower-emission alternative for backup power while supporting grid flexibility.
"Backup power is another major future application of BESS, especially as more data centres look for reliable energy solutions," Chua said.
PUC, meanwhile, plans to use the acquisition as a springboard to build capabilities beyond importing and installing battery systems, with ambitions to develop local assembly and eventually manufacturing capacity.

Title: Ignoring the noise when investing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Investing in stocks is often portrayed as an activity that requires constant attention. Social media, market commentators and investment websites generate a continuous stream of news, opinions, predictions and price movements.
A falling market is accompanied by alarming headlines, while a rising market produces excitement and forecasts of even greater gains. For the long-term investor, however, much of this information is simply noise.
Successful investing requires the discipline to distinguish temporary market fluctuations from genuine changes in a company's underlying fundamentals.
Noise can be defined as information that creates attention or emotional reactions without materially affecting the intrinsic value or long-term prospects of a business.
Daily movements in share prices, rumours, analyst upgrades or downgrades, short-term economic forecasts and sensational headlines may influence investor sentiment, but they do not necessarily change the quality or value of a company.
An investor who reacts to every piece of news risks turning a long-term investment strategy into a series of emotional and often costly trading decisions.
The key principle is simple: an investor should consider taking action when the facts that originally justified the investment have materially changed, not merely because the share price has moved.
Suppose an investor purchases shares in a company because it has a strong balance sheet, growing revenue, consistent cash flow, capable management, a sustainable competitive advantage and attractive long-term growth prospects.
A 10 per cent or 20 per cent decline in the share price, by itself, does not necessarily invalidate the investment thesis. If the company's earnings power, financial strength and competitive position remain intact, the lower share price may simply reflect a change in market sentiment rather than a deterioration in the business.
In fact, one of the greatest mistakes investors make is confusing a change in price with a change in value. A company's share price can fluctuate significantly from day to day because of fear, optimism, interest-rate expectations, geopolitical events or the actions of short-term traders.
Its intrinsic value, however, usually changes more slowly. The underlying value of a business is determined by its ability to generate sustainable cash flows and profits over time. Unless something has changed in those fundamental drivers, a temporary decline in the share price should not automatically trigger a decision to sell.
Conversely, investors should not ignore bad news merely because they are committed to holding a stock for the long term. Long-term investing does not mean holding a company forever regardless of circumstances. Investors must be prepared to act when the fundamentals genuinely deteriorate.
A company may lose its competitive advantage, accumulate excessive debt, suffer persistent declines in profitability, face serious governance failures or experience a permanent disruption to its business model. Such developments may require the investor to reassess the original investment thesis.
For example, declining sales caused by a temporary economic slowdown may be less significant than declining sales caused by customers permanently shifting to a superior competitor or technology.
A short-term reduction in earnings due to higher input costs may be manageable, while a sustained collapse in profit margins may indicate a more serious structural problem.
The important task for the investor is to investigate the cause of the change rather than reacting mechanically to the numbers or headlines.
This approach requires investors to have a clear investment thesis before purchasing a stock. They should know why they own the business, what assumptions support their valuation and which factors could prove them wrong.
A written investment thesis can be particularly useful. It might identify the company's expected growth drivers, competitive strengths, financial risks and valuation assumptions.
When significant news emerges, the investor can then ask a rational question: Does this information materially change my original thesis?
If the answer is no, there may be no reason to act. If the answer is yes, further analysis may be required.
Ignoring noise is also important because excessive activity can be expensive. Frequent buying and selling may generate broking costs and the risk of repeatedly making poor timing decisions.
More importantly, constant trading encourages investors to focus on short-term price movements rather than business performance. The desire to "do something" can become an enemy of good investment decisions. Sometimes the most intelligent action is to remain patient.
Emotional discipline is therefore a critical part of successful investing. Fear can cause investors to sell good companies during temporary market declines, while greed and excitement can encourage them to buy overvalued stocks during periods of euphoria.
Social media can intensify these emotions by creating a sense of urgency and fear of missing out. Investors should remember that markets reward patience more consistently than constant reaction.
This does not mean investors should ignore information. On the contrary, they should monitor their investments carefully by reviewing financial statements, earnings quality, cash flows, debt levels, management decisions and changes in the competitive environment.
The objective is not to become uninformed but to become selective. Investors should filter information through the lens of what truly affects the long-term economics of the business.
Ultimately, successful stock investing is not about predicting every market movement or responding to every headline.
It is about owning sound businesses at sensible prices and periodically reassessing whether the original investment case remains valid. Share prices will fluctuate, markets will overreact and opinions will constantly change. Fundamentals, however, remain the anchor.
The disciplined investor therefore learns to disregard the noise, control emotional reactions and act only when the underlying facts change. In investing, patience is not passive. It is an active decision to remain focused on what matters most: the long-term value and fundamental strength of the business.

Title: Boeing ordered to pay US$29mil to family of 737 MAX crash victim
Article:
NEW YORK: A Chicago jury awarded US$29 million in damages to the family of an Irish-born United Nations employee who died in a 2019 Boeing 737 MAX crash, a US court spokesman said Wednesday.
The civil suit was brought against Boeing by Naoise Connolly Ryan, widow of Michael "Mick" Ryan, an engineer with the UN World Food Programme who was one of the victims in the Ethiopian Airlines crash that killed all 157 people on board.
Ryan had worked during the Ebola crisis in Liberia and with Rohingya refugees. A UN memorial page to Ryan, who was 39 at the time of the crash, also recognised his work Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Ethiopia.
The case is one of the final remaining civil suits pending against Boeing following the pair of deadly MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 that together claimed 346 lives.
The vast majority of claims have been settled out of court with undisclosed terms, but Naoise Ryan's attorney Steven Marks had described his client as "committed to seeking accountability and justice from a jury and not accepting money from Boeing directly."
Boeing has apologised for the crashes and acknowledged that anti-stall software was implicated in both accidents.
Boeing did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In May, a Chicago jury awarded US$49.5 million in damages to the family of Samya Stumo, a 24-year-old American who was killed on the same Ethiopian Airlines flight.--AFP

Title: Credible missile threat prompted secret Trump aircraft switch
Article:
WASHINGTON: A threat that Air Force One could be targeted by a shoulder-fired missile prompted the Secret Service to secretly move President Donald Trump onto a smaller government jet during a trip to Turkiye last month, a person briefed on the matter said on Wednesday.
The threat emerged on the final day of Trump's visit to Ankara for the Nato summit amid heightened tensions with Iran, the source said. The Secret Service deemed the threat to be credible and imminent, prompting an extraordinary operation to conceal the US president's movements.
The source declined to say where the intelligence came from but said officials had little time to prepare and devised the plans at the last minute.
A second source briefed on the matter said there was not a clear plan by those hostile to Trump for executing the threat, but only an intent, which is why the planes were allowed to fly.
Trump and a small group of aides used a catering truck to surreptitiously switch from the big blue-and-white presidential aircraft to a smaller, nondescript C-32A jet for the flight out of Turkiye on July 8, while Air Force One departed separately carrying senior administration officials, White House staff and the traveling press corps, according to the first source.
Trump told reporters on Tuesday that he made the switch at the direction of the Secret Service, which is charged with presidential security. He flew from Ankara to a refueling stop in Britain without incident.
"I think actually the plane that I flew on was at greater risk," Trump told reporters, without providing evidence. "I think it was at ​greater risk because that would be the plane I think that they would be more likely to go for."
The threat may have been a new type of heat-seeking missile that homes in on hot aircraft engines and has become an increasing concern for military planners, said Douglas Birkey, executive director of the Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies.
They are harder to detect than traditional radar-guided threats and "can kind of come out of nowhere" because they don't send out detectable radio waves. One version, the Iranian SA-67, has a simple rail launcher and is believed to use heat-seeking as well as laser guidance systems, Birkey said. A shoulder-mounted heat-seeking weapon, the 9K333 Verba, is made in Russia, he said.
SECRET TRAVEL
US presidents, including Trump, have occasionally traveled under secrecy when visiting war zones or high-risk regions in order to maintain security.
But those trips typically involved advance notice for journalists traveling with the president. Some members of the press got a heads-up ahead of a Thanksgiving 2003 trip by President George W. Bush to Baghdad. Other members of the press corps covering Bush's Thanksgiving holiday in Crawford, Texas, were misled, however.
Told that Bush was spending the feast day with family, they were shocked when the president abruptly surfaced in Iraq. The first source on Wednesday said the Secret Service did not have the luxury of time in Turkiye.
"They were scrambling to head off what they thought was a credible, imminent threat," the source said.
The Washington Post first reported details of the operation this week, more than a month after it was carried out.
The New York Times reported that US officials were alarmed to discover that Iranians knew where Trump was staying in Ankara, including the exact floor of his hotel.
On board the Air Force One jet now seen as a decoy were US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who the first source said was briefed on the maneuver; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent; White House communications director Steven Cheung; and a number of other aides plus the typical 13-person press pool that included a Reuters correspondent and photographer.
White House deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino, executive assistant Natalie Harp and director of Oval Office operations Walt Nauta made the move in the catering truck with Trump, the source said.
Some media commentators ⁠and lawmakers have questioned whether the operation left Trump's aides and journalists traveling with him at risk aboard the plane presumed to be carrying the ​president.
The first source said it was determined that it was in Trump's best interests to keep the ruse secret as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Turkiye.
Turkish officials did not immediately comment on the threat.--REUTERS

Title: Tabung Haji tightens fund oversight, investment monitoring
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   Tabung Haji is reviewing its framework in overseeing and monitoring its funds and investment management to strengthen its governance according to the Tabung Haji Act 1995.
The pilgrimage fund said in a statement yesterday the review  required more comprehensive assessment and cooperation with relevant stakeholders.
The improvements would be implemented in an orderly manner, taking into account the respective jurisdictions, legislative processes and appropriate timelines, it added.
The move was significant given that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) had recommended reforms to Tabung Haji's governance and investment framework.
They included greater separation of responsibilities over haj management and financial matters, funds and investments.
The RCI also proposed that Tabung Haji's investment function be managed through a dedicated department, known as Dana Haji, which would remain within the fund, but registered or licensed by the Securities Commission.
Tabung Haji did not specify when the review of the act would be completed, saying it would proceed according to the relevant legislative process and timeline.
FINAL REFINEMENT
Tabung Haji said it is at the final stage of refining its haj management policy to provide a clearer, more structured and systematic pathway for performing the pilgrimage.
"This approach places emphasis on the concept of istito'ah, including financial readiness and early planning, so that more Muslims can prepare sustainably to perform the haj," it said.
Tabung Haji is now focused on strengthening the institution and ensuring that reforms deliver tangible benefits to depositors and prospective pilgrims.
STRENGTHENED POSITION
Tabung Haji said reforms to date have covered key areas including its financial position, governance and accountability, risk management, accounting standards, investment portfolio restructuring, and greater financial and profit distribution discipline.
"The results of these reforms can be seen in Tabung Haji's position today. Its balance sheet has been strengthened, with assets exceeding liabilities, financial reserves continuing to build, while investments are managed through a more disciplined approach based on controlled risk.
"In 2025, Tabung Haji recorded investment income of RM4.64 billion and distributed RM3.22 billion in profits at a rate of 3.5 per cent to more than 9.7 million depositors, the highest distribution rate in eight years," it said.
RISING DEPOSITS
The pilgrimage fund said confidence in the institution should be assessed based on its  financial position and performance.
"Depositors' savings have grown significantly from about RM69.4 billion in 2019 to more than RM95 billion in 2026.
"Movements in deposits are part of the normal activities of a savings institution, and Tabung Haji monitors these developments closely.
"More importantly, Tabung Haji's financial fundamentals remain strong, while the interests and security of depositors' savings continue to be the priority in every decision made," it said.
Tabung Haji said the cost of performing the haj  had been maintained for three consecutive seasons, while the quality of its pilgrim management had received international recognition through the Labaytum Diamond Award for two consecutive years.
On investigations being conducted by the authorities, Tabung Haji said it fully respects the processes and jurisdictions, and would provide the necessary cooperation when required.
"Tabung Haji will not speculate or pre-empt any ongoing process. Its focus remains on its responsibility as an institution entrusted to manage Muslims' savings and facilitate the performance of the haj,"
Tabung Haji said it would continue to communicate important developments on its reform and improvement efforts through the appropriate channels once they are finalised.

Title: Trump authorises cyber operations targeting transnational crime groups
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump signed a memo on Wednesday that the White House said was aimed at empowering federal law enforcement to use cyber tools against transnational criminal organisations that operate in foreign jurisdictions to attack Americans.
Trump signed the national security presidential memorandum directing his administration to "leverage the capability and innovation of the private sector to help conduct these cyber operations under the direction, control, and authority of the US Government," the White House said.
The White House, in a fact sheet about the memo, cited ransomware attacks, financial frauds and other crimes run by foreign-based organised criminal organizations. The memo creates a framework that encourages private sector companies to enter into agreements with other private entities, as well as federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial agencies to gather threat information on transnational criminal organisations and propose cyber operations to address those threats, the White House added. --REUTERS

Title: Expert: 'Kootu' scheme contributors not automatically offenders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Joining a
kootu
scheme does not necessarily make a person an offender,  a banking law expert said.
Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM) School of Law senior lecturer Dr Muhammad Hafiz Badarulzaman said the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971 primarily targeted those who operated or promoted
kootu
funds as a business.
He said businesses set up to promote
kootu
funds could not be registered under the Registration of Businesses Act 1956.
"Companies are also prohibited from being registered under the Companies Act 2016  if one of their objectives is to promote
kootu
funds," he told the
New Straits Times.
He said traditional
kootu
arrangements without profit, interest or membership fees were not prohibited under the  Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971.
However, he said
kootu
contributors could  expose themselves to legal action if  they  promoted or helped to organise it.
Under Section 2 of the act, he said, the definition of "promoting" includes managing, organising, aiding, assisting or taking part in the promotion of a
kootu
fund.
Hafiz said contributors involved in large-scale commercial
kootu
schemes could  face investigation where the scheme involved an illegal money game or fraud.
He, however, said any proposal to impose criminal liability on ordinary contributors required  consideration, as such participants could themselves  be victims.
He said criminalising ordinary contributors across the board would  be impractical, while existing laws could  be used where a contributor was also found to have abetted or been complicit in an offence.
Hafiz said the existing legal framework under the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act  was  broad enough to cover
kootu
schemes operated   online.
Section 2 defines a
kootu
as  "scheme or arrangement" involving participants contributing to a  pool which is  paid out according to an agreed method, without restricting the medium through which the arrangement is organised.
He cited a 2022 case in which a trader was fined RM50,000 by the Butterworth Sessions Court after pleading guilty to promoting a
kootu
fund through Facebook involving five participants and transactions amounting to RM100,000.
"The existing legal framework can deal with online
kootu
schemes. The more important issue is  enforcement and  ensuring  the law distinguishes between commercial promoters and ordinary contributors."

Title: Wong Chen exit exposes deeper challenge for PKR, say analysts [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wong Chen's exit from PKR may not necessarily affect the party's standing in the urban Subang parliamentary constituency, but it signals a deeper challenge for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's party, say analysts.
International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) political analyst Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said PKR must now re-examine its identity and future direction following Wong's departure to Parti Bersama Malaysia.
"For PKR, this means they are losing their reformist faction. The party needs to figure out what it wants to be and where it wants to go from here.
"As for Subang, I think the seat is still safe for PKR. Under the PKR banner, Wong won over 100,000 votes, and I don't think half of those voters will abandon PKR to vote for him in Bersama," Syaza told the New Straits Times.
She said other PKR figures, such as Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung and Ampang MP Rodziah Ismail, could eventually follow in Wong's footsteps, although she believed any further departures were more likely towards the end of the parliamentary term.
Universiti Malaya sociopolitical analyst Professor Datuk Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said Wong's departure hurt PKR "symbolically more than numerically" for now.
"The bigger danger to PKR is if Bersama begins attracting its urban reformist voter base, not simply its MPs," he said.
Awang Azman said Wong's move strengthened the impression that Bersama was becoming a political home for the Rafizi-aligned, reformist and policy-oriented faction of PKR.
Still, Awang Azman said PH should still be considered the favourites in Subang, but Wong could make Bersama highly competitive if he contests.
In the 15th General Election, Wong secured 138,259 votes, or 77.7 per cent of votes cast, winning with a majority of 115,074.
"My assessment is that much of that vote belonged to the PH ecosystem rather than Wong alone.
"However, if Bersama successfully frames itself as the new reform movement while PH suffers further dissatisfaction, Subang could become one of Bersama's best urban targets," Awang Azman said.
Universiti Sains Malaysia political analyst Professor Datuk Dr Sivamurugan Pandian similarly did not expect Wong's departure to trigger an immediate wave of defections.
He said Wong's resignation reflected internal dissatisfaction and weakening cohesion within PKR, and could embolden other members unhappy with the party's leadership or direction.
Universiti Malaya's Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Wong's exit did not necessarily mean PKR was collapsing, but raised questions about the party's reformist credentials.
"It raises an important question over whether the party can continue to retain voters who supported it because of its reform agenda, especially if more prominent figures leave," Tawfik said.

Title: MAHA 2026 to focus on smart farming and automation
Article:
SERDANG: Smart farming, automation and agricultural technology will take centre stage at MAHA 2026 as Malaysia steps up efforts to strengthen food security and boost productivity across the agri-food sector.
Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak said this year's exhibition would place greater emphasis on technology, innovation, processing and marketing, rather than just agricultural production.
He said this was in line with the theme of MAHA 2026, "Penciptaan Nilai Demi Keterjaminan Makanan" (Value Creation for Food Security).
"The agri-food sector can no longer be viewed from the perspective of production alone.
"It must also encompass technology, innovation, processing and marketing," he said during a media briefing on MAHA 2026, here, yesterday.
Isham said the government wanted to ensure every stage of the agri-food supply chain generated greater value while contributing to a more resilient and sustainable national food system.
He said the push for modern technology and automation was  important as Malaysia sought to increase productivity and strengthen food security without  solely  expanding agricultural land.
MAHA 2026, to be held at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang from Aug 28 to Sept 6, is expected to attract about four million visitors and feature around 2,000 exhibitors from Malaysia and abroad.
Isham said the exhibition would showcase the latest developments in smart agriculture and digitalisation, including through its agrotech and young agropreneur segments.
He said the government also wanted to attract more youths to the sector by demonstrating that agriculture offered significant economic and career opportunities.
"We want to attract more youths to see the agri-food sector as a sector of the future with significant economic and career potential."
MAHA 2026 will also feature an Immersive agrotech segment in Hall C.
Hall A will focus on international trade, including MAHA Go Global, international country pavilions, the Exporter's Club and the Hosted Buyer Programme.
Fourteen countries, including the United States, Japan, South Korea, China, Brazil and the Netherlands, will participate in the international country pavilions.
The event will also bring together 40 international buyers with Malaysian exhibitors whose products are ready for export.
Isham said the initiatives were intended to turn MAHA into more than an exhibition by creating opportunities for local businesses to expand into international markets.
He said the government was targeting RM8 billion in potential investments through memoranda of understanding and agreements, alongside RM58 million in direct sales.
"MAHA is no longer just an exhibition. We want it to become a platform for the economy, innovation and national food security."
Isham said the wider objective was to ensure MAHA left a longer-term impact on the country's agri-food ecosystem through greater technology adoption, stronger industry networks, youth participation and expanded export opportunities.

Title: Fadhlina: Teach children to speak up, disagree respectfully
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
CHILDREN should not only be taught to be well-behaved, but also to have the confidence to speak up, think critically and disagree respectfully, said Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek.
She said character education was needed to train them to articulate their views, challenge opposing opinions and defend their positions without compromising courtesy.
"Character education is not just about teaching children to be good. We want them to be brave to speak up, think critically and remain respectful even when they have differing views.
"This is the character education that we need," she said in a Facebook post after attending the national-level Madani Youth Forum yesterday.
"What happened on stage was much bigger than a competition. These children were learning how to think before they speak, organise their thoughts, state their positions, listen to different views and defend their arguments."
Fadhlina said the forum demonstrated how young people could also build confidence in using Bahasa Melayu while developing their ability to argue and engage with diverse perspectives.
She added that efforts to uphold Bahasa Melayu should focus on giving young people more opportunities to use the language.
She also said a mature nation was not built by a generation that agreed on everything, but by one that knew how to disagree constructively.
"Our task is not to determine what they should say. It is to ensure that when it is their turn to speak, they have the knowledge to argue and the courtesy to listen," she added.

Title: Trump sued over paid early access to market-moving Truth Social posts
Article:
NEW YORK: Donald Trump was sued on Wednesday by two media entities seeking to shut down a new service that sells paid access to the US president's posts, including some that can move markets, on his Truth Social platform.
The complaint filed in Manhattan federal court by the Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation challenges Truth API, a feed offered by Trump Media & Technology Group that charges up to US$100,000 a month for early access to 10 high-profile Truth Social accounts, including Trump's own.
Truth API launched on August 1, four days after Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California called on the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether it undermined the integrity of financial markets while enriching Wall Street, wealthy insiders and Trump.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Other White House officials are also defendants but Trump Media is not.
Trump has long used Truth Social to disclose news, such as on tariffs and Middle East conflicts, that can move prices of stocks, oil and other markets.
Wednesday's lawsuit seeks to block the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social while the paid feed exists.
PLAINTIFFS CALL SERVICE 'PROFOUNDLY CORRUPT'
In the complaint, the plaintiffs called the Truth API service "profoundly corrupt" because the president stands to gain financially when subscribers sign up.
They also said the service violated the US Constitution's First Amendment because everyone deserved equal access to Trump's announcements, and there was no legitimate government interest in selling Trump's posts to private subscribers and letting him profit.
According to the complaint, many of Trump's 9,000 to 11,000 Truth Social posts and reposts during his second White House term were never followed by official White House statements.
A Trump Media spokesperson said "countless" platforms and news outlets, including many offering subscription feeds, already disseminate information from Trump, a Republican.
"Now, left-wing activists are trying to wrongfully weaponise the courts to censor him" and harm shareholders, the spokesperson said.
On an earnings call on Monday, Trump Media interim Chief Executive Kevin McGurn said Truth API enabled subscribers to get news "fractionally faster" than others.
TRUMP IS LARGEST SHAREHOLDER
The president is Trump Media's largest shareholder, with a 41.3pct stake worth approximately US$950 million through his Donald J. Trump Revocable Trust, Reuters data show.
His oldest son Donald Trump Jr. is a Trump Media director and oversees the trust. Other accounts offered through Truth API include those of Vice President JD Vance, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., FBI Director Kash Patel and the White House itself, the complaint said.
The SEC's three current commissioners are Republican. --REUTERS

Title: Govt to boost airport security, border cooperation
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
COMPREHENSIVE plan to improve airport security will be tabled at the cabinet meeting next week.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said yesterday the plan would cover agency coordination, personnel training, infrastructure and logistics, with a focus on screening procedures and equipment operators.
He said the government viewed seriously the issue of drugs passing through airports.
"Yesterday (Tuesday), various agencies held a meeting. I was informed that a paper on proposed improvements will be presented to the cabinet within a week."
He added that the review would also cover airport scanners, closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera systems and procedures for handling items detected during screening.
He said this issue was not about how many CCTV cameras there were — Kuala Lumpur International Airport has 5,000 — but whether there were blind spots and if personnel were adequately trained.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin said several countries, including the United States and Japan, had revised their travel advisories on Sabah following significant security improvements over the past three years.
He said this would boost tourist arrivals, particularly along Sabah's east coast, which was overseen by the Eastern Sabah Security Command.
However, he said, Malaysia would continue efforts to convince more nations of Sabah's safety, including inviting ambassadors to visit and observe the security situation first-hand.
On another note, Malaysia and Thailand were stepping up cooperation to prevent cross-border crime and monitor movements along their shared frontier, said Saifuddin.
Both countries had government-to-government and police-to-police mechanisms, including a joint committee that meets twice a year and cooperation involving police in Perlis, Kedah and Kelantan.
On claims that unrest in Thailand had resulted in criminals fleeing to Malaysia, Saifuddin said the government was aware of the security implications of cross-border movement.
"These issues are being addressed through established channels. We do not resolve them through media statements, but through appropriate platforms and forums, in keeping with the conduct expected between neighbouring countries," he added.

Title: Karoline Leavitt to step down as Trump's press secretary
Article:
WASHINGTON: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who earned a reputation for acid putdowns of journalists, is to step down, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday adding she would remain a senior advisor.
Leavitt, 28, the youngest ever US presidential top spokesperson, has been a fiercely loyal Trump defender, delivering fluent and aggressive performances at often combative press briefings.
"Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family," Trump said on social media.
"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party."
In May, Leavitt announced the birth of her second child – a girl named Viviana – just days after delaying her maternity leave following an alleged assassination attempt on Trump when a gunman tried to storm the White House correspondents dinner.
Her departure, just weeks after returning to the job, comes as Trump faces steadily sinking poll numbers and the Republican Party risks defeat in the November midterm congressional elections.
"I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium," Leavitt said on social media as her departure was announced.
"I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump's successes."
Leavitt wrote that after returning to the White House after the birth of her daughter, "I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve" while devoting the attention needed as press secretary.
Leavitt, is a Trump veteran who served in his press office during his first term that ended in 2021 and then as his spokesperson during his 2024 election campaign.
Leavitt's tenure as press secretary saw a revival of regular briefings that had petered out during the first term, but she presided over sea change on White House interactions with journalists.
In February 2025, she stunned the press corps when she announced that the White House itself – and not an independent association of correspondents – would choose which reporters got to cover Trump up close in the Oval Office and on Air Force One.
She also facilitated press credentials from right-wing, pro-Trump media outlets, diluting the presence of traditional news media that tend to ask more challenging questions in the briefing room.
Raised in New Hampshire, where her family ran an ice cream shop, Leavitt sent a letter to her university newspaper in 2017 to protest against the fact that a professor had criticized Trump in class.
After Trump's 2020 election loss, She unsuccessfully ran for a seat in Congress in New Hampshire in 2022 on a pro-Trump, pro-gun ownership platform.
She then won his praise for steely television performances during his 2024 re-election campaign.
She signaled her intent to pursue a political path, stating "our country is facing an existential threat from an increasingly extremist Democrat Party that seeks to destroy everything great about America."
"My fight is entering a new phase, but it is far from over."--AFP

Title: Milky Mist's US$163m IPO fully subscribed
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
BENGALURU: Temasek-backed Milky Mist Dairy Food's nearly US$163 million initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed on the second day of a three-day bidding process yesterday, led by retail and non-institutional investors.
The dairy products maker received bids for 86.88 million shares as of 10.48 am IST — 1.06 times the 81.80 million shares on offer — exchange data showed.
The company raised 4.65 billion rupees from 19 anchor investors, including Singapore state investor Temasek, the International Finance Corporation and HDFC Mutual Fund, ahead of the IPO.
The 15.53 billion rupees (US$162.96 million) IPO comprises a fresh issue worth 14.28 billion rupees and an offer for sale worth 1.25 billion rupees by founders Sathishkumar T and Anitha S.
The company cut the IPO size from 20.35 billion rupees after pre-listing deals with Temasek's Jongsong Investments, which acquired a roughly 5.2 per cent stake in the company.
Milky Mist is seeking a valuation of about 107.78 billion rupees (US$1.13 billion) at the top end of its price range of 133-140 rupees per share, just over half the market value of larger rival Hatsun Agro Product.
The dairy products maker's portfolio includes cheese, butter, ice cream, Greek yoghurt and protein-enhanced cottage cheese.
It plans to use part of the IPO proceeds to repay debt and to upgrade and expand its main manufacturing plant in Perundurai, Tamil Nadu.
Milky Mist's profit rose about 176 per cent to 1.27 billion rupees in the year ended March 31. — REUTERS

Title: Rob Reiner son denies grand jury murder charges
Article:
LOS ANGELES: The son of legendary US film director Rob Reiner denied new charges of killing both his parents when he appeared in court on Wednesday after grand jury indictments were unsealed.
Nick Reiner pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder, with the special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and murder by means of lying in wait.
The charges supercede the previous ones that were filed over the December 2025 double slaying of his filmmaker father and his photographer mother Michele Singer.
The 32-year-old was arrested on December 14 after his parents' bloodied bodies were discovered at their home in the affluent Brentwood neighborhood of Los Angeles.
Rob Reiner, 79 – who directed huge hits including "When Harry Met Sally" and "A Few Good Men" – and his wife, 70, were stabbed to death.
Nick Reiner, who has a history of addiction and remains in jail, was ordered to return to court on September 15.
"This was a profound betrayal by someone who was loved and trusted by the very people he is accused of killing," Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said.
"The indictment unsealed today also adds a special circumstance allegation that the defendant committed the murders by means of lying in wait.
"We hope that by having a grand jury return an indictment in this case it will bring us one step closer to a trial and achieving justice."
If convicted as charged, Nick Reiner could face life in prison without parole, or the death penalty, although California does not routinely carry out capital punishment.
Nick Reiner, who lived in a guest house on his parents' property, had attended a party at the home of comedian Conan O'Brien on December 13 with his parents, where some attendees reportedly said he had behaved erratically.
Rob Reiner, the son of legendary comedian Carl Reiner, started his showbiz career in acting.
He won fame as the oafish son-in-law Michael "Meathead" Stivic on groundbreaking 1970s sitcom "All in the Family," before transitioning to directing.
As a director, his output included classic films like 1984's rock music mockumentary "This is Spinal Tap," fantasy gem "The Princess Bride" from 1987, and seminal coming-of-age movie "Stand By Me."--AFP

Title: Global youth unemployment at 12.4pc in 2025, says ILO
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
GLOBAL youth unemployment increased last year as weaker economic growth, geopolitical tensions and sluggish job creation made it harder for young people to find work, said the International Labour Organisation (ILO) yesterday.
It also warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could add to mounting labour market pressures.
The global unemployment rate among 15- to 24-year-olds rose to 12.4 per cent last year from 12.3 per cent in 2023, equivalent to 67 million people, according to a new report by the United Nations labour agency.
This marked a reversal of improvements seen after the Covid-19 pandemic, said the report.
The ILO said the share of young people not in employment, education or training  also edged higher to 20 per cent, representing more than 257 million people.
"The picture is worsening almost universally," the report added, noting that youth unemployment increased between 2023 and last year  in eight of the world's 11 sub-regions.
Youth unemployment was highest in the Arab States at 26.2 per cent, followed by Northern Africa at 22.6 per cent.
Some of the sharpest deterioration occurred in wealthier economies, with youth unemployment in North America climbing to 9.8 per cent from 8.3 per cent in 2023.
Across Northern, Southern and Western Europe, the rate stood at 15 per cent.
The agency highlighted the decline of middle-skilled jobs that had traditionally provided an entry point into the labour market for young people leaving secondary school or university.
The trend could intensify as AI transformed workplaces, it said.
The ILO estimated that 6.1 per cent of jobs currently held by people aged 15 to 29 were in occupations most exposed to AI-related changes.
If just 10 per cent of those jobs disappeared entirely, around 5.6 million young workers, mainly in high-income countries, could face unemployment, career changes or exit the labour force, it said.
At the same time, jobs in high-skilled sectors continued to expand in most countries, it added.  — REUTERS

Title: UK 'joke' candidate Binface pushes serious point about politics
Article:
BRITISH politics has a long-cherished reputation for attracting the weird and wonderful. But in a pantheon of colourful characters, Count Binface, a man wearing a rubbish bin over his head, is stealing the show.
The self-described "intergalactic space warrior" from the fictional planet Sigma IX takes on hardline anti-immigrant politician Nigel Farage on Thursday in the Clacton by-election, triggered when the Reform UK leader resigned in a shock move.
With Farage running again for his seat, none of the UK's mainstream political parties is fielding candidates, having dismissed the move as a stunt designed to stall a parliamentary inquiry into his finances.
That has left the door open to Count Binface, and a host of other independent and parody candidates.
While polls give Farage a clear victory with more than 70 per cent of the vote, Binface, the alter ego of comedian and comedy writer Jon Harvey, is grabbing all the attention and could win as much as 20 per cent.
During almost a decade as the joke candidate in UK politics, Binface has fully embraced the absurd.
He arrives at election counts wearing a metallic dustbin-shaped helmet, a silver cape and silver-and-black armour and brandishing his razor-sharp, deadpan sense of humour.
His manifestos mix smart political satire with comedic promises to cap croissant prices, improve WiFi on UK trains and conscript people using speakerphones on public transport.
"In the UK anybody, literally anybody, is free to stand in an election, no matter how idiotic the get-up", he told AFP ahead of the 2024 London mayoral elections.
The British political system "fosters the eccentricity, the wonderment and the humour of politics", he added.
DEMOCRACY MATTERS
Harvey, 46, is a University of Oxford Classics graduate who has written for popular satirical television programmes including "The Thick of It" and "Have I Got News for You."
In a recent appearance on the "The Rest is Politics" podcast, he quoted from Homer's "Odyssey" in fluent Homeric Greek.
He first attracted attention in 2017 as Lord Buckethead, when he challenged then-prime minister Theresa May in the general election.
A copyright dispute later prompted a rebranding, leading to the birth of Count Binface in 2018.
Since then, Binface has contested elections against former prime ministers Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak as well as London mayor Sadiq Khan, consistently drawing thousands of votes and extensive media coverage.
[[nid:1509988]]
In the 2021 London mayoral race, he won 24,775 first-preference ballots – one per cent of the vote – and netted a similar tally at the next vote in 2024, easily beating the far-right Britain First party.
Khan, who won re-election in the 2024 election, paid tribute to Binface for standing, joking the count had made him "work hard for it."
Unlike some novelty candidates, Harvey insists there is a serious point to his activism.
His policy platform often lampoons mainstream politics while drawing on genuine public anger and frustrations, and advocating in support of democracy.
"Behind every one of these campaigns is a simple argument... that a ballot is worth casting even when you know how the night ends," he writes on his website.
'UNITY CANDIDATE'
On Monday, he posted an "interplanetary address" on X which played on a screen attached to a balloon floating at an altitude of 100,000 feet (30,500 metres) above Earth thanks to a specialist company.
"Join me. Let's take out the trash and make 13th of August bin day!" he says.
Other manifesto pledges have included forcing water company bosses to swim in polluted rivers and banning loud snacks in cinemas.
"I pledge to build at least one affordable house," Binface joked in his Clacton manifesto.
He skewers Farage, vowing not to take £5 million gifts from crypto billionaires, and spend more time in Clacton than Washington. He also presents himself as a "unity candidate."
The looming battle between Farage and a candidate with a tongue-in-cheek slogan "Make Earth great again" has triggered huge international media interest.
And as Britain's political landscape fragments, Binface has become more than a comic sideshow.
For Farage, "while it's embarrassing for him to win against a dustbin, and not the mainstream parties, he will return as MP," said Catherine Barnard, a political expert at Cambridge University.
But she added there "are some indications that Nigel Farage is worried that he will not win as comprehensively as he wants to."
Even former prime minister Keir Starmer had one last dig at Farage in parliament, saying: "My advice to everyone is put your vote in the bin."
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Tourists rush to Mount Etna as Italian volcano erupts
Article:
ROME: Spectacular images of lava flowing down the slopes of an erupting Mount Etna have drawn flocks of tourists to the Italian volcano – to the worry of local guides.
The tallest active volcano in Europe, Etna has been spewing ash and lava for days, forcing the closure of the nearby Catania airport, a key gateway for tourists visiting the island of Sicily.
Companies that organise nighttime hikes allowing participants to watch the eruption up close say they have been flooded with calls.
"They all want to come and see the lava flow, everyone is drawn to this unique beauty," Daniele Perricelli, 41, a local guide told AFP on Wednesday.
Perricelli's group, Guide Etna, takes a few dozen visitors up the volcano every evening – but is currently receiving about 300 requests a day, three times what it gets on an average summer day, he said.
Ernesto Maria Magri, another local guide, called it a "touristic eruption" that appeals to "many people" because it can be observed in relative safety.
Even though the volcano erupts frequently, he said many local residents were also climbing up to see the lava and "sometimes crowd round in a disorderly way."
Unwilling or unable to secure a guide, many venture up on their own.
That is potentially risky, said Perricelli, explaining the volcano was unstable and it was important to be with someone who could read the mountain.
"There are up to 2,000 people climbing up every evening, the footpaths are overcrowded," he said. "Yesterday, we saw some wearing flip-flops," he added, calling on authorities to be more vigilant.
Some climbers, including Italian TV host Diletta Leotta, have been criticised on social media for taking photos seemingly too close to glowing lava.
Yet, guides said it is possible to come within a few metres of the volcanic flow in lower altitude areas where it has already cooled down.
Under current rules visitors can climb up to around 2,400 metres of altitude on their own but need to be accompanied by a guide to go higher, tour operators say.
The summit is at 3,324 metres.
Italy's civil protection agency has issued a yellow alert for Etna, the second on a four-step scale going from green to red, which entails frequent eruptions and possible explosions.
Ash emissions have caused Catania airport to repeatedly halt flights over the past few days, with Italian media reporting hundreds of flights have been cancelled since Saturday.
The airport operator said Wednesday arrivals and departures would remain suspended until 4 pm (1400 GMT) on Thursday.
Around 12 million passengers transited in 2024 through Catania International Airport, which services the eastern part of Sicily, one of Italy's most popular tourist destinations.

Title: Trump says US will 'keep' Hormuz strait control
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the United States is in control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz and will "keep it."
"The U.S.A. has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. "Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, 'A WALL OF STEEL,' and there is nothing Iran can do about it."
Trump has repeatedly claimed the United States controls the strait, which is vital for the flow of energy and other commodity shipping through the Middle East.
However, Iran says it effectively controls much of the waterway and intends to impose a toll system in response to the US war launched by Trump on Feb 28.
Late Tuesday, Trump told reporters: "We have total control over the Hormuz Strait right now. They don't have control. We have total control. We own it."
US and Israeli forces have heavily bombed Iran's military and killed a swath of the country's leadership so far in the nearly six month war, launched initially with goals including forcing Tehran to abandon its nuclear power program and regime change.
Iran has resisted with missile attacks on US bases in the region, Israel and targets in US-allied Gulf countries.
Its most effective response has been to strike shipping in Hormuz, effectively snarling the trade route, rattling the world economy.
With his political popularity sinking at home ahead of the November midterm congressional elections, Trump has backed off threats to escalate the war in search of a decisive victory.
That leaves the war in a standoff.
However, the Republican says that the United States is prepared to focus on blockading Iranian ports in a strategy that he told Axios was "low-keying."
"We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money," Trump told Axios on Sunday.

Title: Zhu Rongji, trailblazing ex-premier who transformed China's economy
Article:
ZHU Rongji, China's former premier who died on Wednesday aged 97, championed free-market policies and delivered far-reaching economic reforms during his five years at the helm.
Rumoured to be descended from Zhu Yuanzhang, the founding emperor of the Ming dynasty, Zhu was born in the central city of Changsha in 1928 into a China riven by civil war.
Zhu studied electrical engineering at Beijing's elite Tsinghua University and joined the Communist Party in 1949, the same year leader Mao Zedong declared the creation of the "New China."
An economic planner and later an engineer at the State Planning Commission, Zhu was purged twice during the tumultuous early decades of the People's Republic.
He was first cast out during the "Hundred Flowers Campaign" in the 1950s, when his criticism of Mao's "irrational" economic policies saw him labelled a "rightist."
He was pardoned but purged again during the chaos and bloodshed of the Cultural Revolution, when he was sent into exile in rural China.
The party rehabilitated him in the wake of Mao's death, tapping him for jobs at the Ministry of Petroleum and State Economic Commission.
His talents caught the eye of then-paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and in 1988 he was appointed mayor of China's economic powerhouse city Shanghai, where he developed a reputation as a stalwart supporter of market reform.
In a speech that year, he called for state-owned enterprises to be allowed to "swim by themselves in the markets."
Appointed vice premier under then-leader Jiang Zemin in 1991, he found himself nicknamed China's Mikhail Gorbachev after the reformist former president of the Soviet Union.
He was seen as largely responsible for China's "soft landing" – reducing inflation without causing a recession – after it experienced runaway growth following Deng's renewed push to open up in the 1990s.
But it was his radical reforms as premier from 1998 that cemented his reputation as a no-compromise free marketeer.
Among those was a broad programme to privatise unprofitable state-owned enterprises – long a guarantee of lifelong so-called "iron rice bowl" employment for millions but which drained public finances.
Those reforms slashed 30 million jobs over five years, leaving workers at the mercy of cutthroat market forces that spurred massive growth but which massively exacerbated economic inequality.
He also oversaw the privatisation of urban housing, scrapping welfare for millions of urban workers and promoting home ownership.
Those reforms sparked a boom in real estate and construction, which would soar to become a quarter of China's economy before a crippling debt crisis struck in 2020.
His leadership was credited with helping China avoid the worst of the 1997 Asian financial crisis, bucking a global trend.
[[nid:1509979]]
And he led negotiations for China's accession to the World Trade Organisation in 2001 – a move seen as consolidating the country's transformation from an isolated economy under Mao to the marketplace of the world.
Zhu also developed a reputation as a hard-nosed opponent of corruption, which he once described as one of China's most pressing problems.
During his tenure, a former vice governor of eastern Jiangxi province was executed for taking bribes, the highest-ranking official to be put to death for such charges in five decades.
A fluent English speaker, he formalised the traditional premier's press conference at the end of the yearly "Two Sessions" political meet.
During those meetings he was known for tackling questions head-on, with a sardonic sense of humour.
At his debut press conference, he vowed to face down "multitudinous minefields and 30,000-metre abysses" in reforming China.
In retirement, "Boss Zhu" published a number of books of speeches on economic reform, and was listed as one of the country's top philanthropists.
But his brand of market reformism, which lifted millions out of poverty but unleashed inequality, fell out of vogue with the ascent of Xi Jinping, China's most powerful leader in generations, in 2012.
Xi has since condemned runaway capitalism and sought to move China onto a more balanced development path, as well as cracking down on excessive displays of wealth and private firms seen as monopolistic.
And under Xi, Zhu's style of open, frank talk by officials has been replaced by a much more staid, closed-off approach.
The late former premier notably clashed with the current leadership over Xi's consolidation of power and statist approach in 2022, The Wall Street Journal reported.
In office, Zhu was asked by a Danish reporter what he hoped the Chinese people would remember him for.
"I only hope that after I step down, people across the country will say that 'he was an honest official, not a corrupt one' and I'll be very satisfied with that," he said.
"If they are a bit more generous and say that 'Zhu Rongji did accomplish some practical things', I will thank the heavens."
Zhu is survived by his wife, Lao An and two children.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 15-year-old boy drowns while swimming in river
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 15-year-old boy drowned while swimming with friends in a river near Masjid Ulu Pulai, Kampung Ulu Pulai, Gelang Patah, yesterday.
Pekan Nanas Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Md Bakhtiar Chik said the department received an emergency call at 6.15pm.
He said 17 firefighters, assisted by four fire engines, were deployed to the scene, about 15km away.
"The victim was believed to have gone to the river with four friends to swim.
"He was believed to have disappeared while diving," he said in a statement.
Bakhtiar said members of the public initially searched the water after learning that the boy was missing.
He said the Water Rescue Team later conducted a dive and found the victim at the bottom of the river, about 4m deep and 2m from the riverbank.
"The victim was found at 10.05pm before the body was handed over to police for further action.
"The search and rescue operation ended at 10.30pm," he said.

Title: Soldier injured by fellow serviceman's shot at Port Dickson firing range
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A soldier was injured after he was believed to have been hit by a shot fired by a fellow serviceman at a firing range in Sungai Menyala, Port Dickson, yesterday.
Negri Sembilan deputy police chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Nasharudin Mohd Shariff said police received a report on the incident, which occurred at 2.15pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was at the firing range with several other personnel when he was believed to have been hit by a shot fired by a fellow serviceman.
"The victim sustained facial injuries and was taken to Port Dickson Hospital for initial treatment before being referred to Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital, Seremban, for further examination and treatment.
"He is reported to be in stable condition," he said in a statement.
Nasharudin said police had arrested a man in his 20s, also a soldier, to assist in the investigation.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 37 of the Arms Act 1960 for causing injury with a firearm without lawful excuse and Section 337 of the Penal Code for causing hurt by an act endangering life or the personal safety of others.
"Further investigations are underway to determine the actual cause of the incident," he said.

Title: French buyers rethinking housing choices after heatwaves
Article:
AFTER multiple severe heatwaves in a single summer, French residents are increasingly factoring high temperatures into their home hunts, realtors say, bumping up features such as shutters, air conditioning and indirect sunlight on their priority lists.
In Paris this summer, steep temperatures turned apartments directly under iconic Haussmann-era buildings with zinc-covered roofs into virtual ovens.
"On the top floor of a Haussmann-style building, the heat indoors can become truly unbearable," said Joseph Denke, an estate agent with FredeLion in Paris.
He has noted a shift in buyers' priorities in recent months, including being wary of south-facing windows.
The heat risk in a studio apartment under the eaves with no through air — windows on just one side for example — was a negative point for Camille Couturier during a viewing with Denke.
"We're seeing that heatwaves are happening in June or even May," the 30-year-old said.
For his future flat, he is thinking "10 to 15 years ahead" and is concerned about whether he will be able to "live comfortably in it" or end up "having to flee like everyone else because it's too hot".
According to a study by Pouget Consultants and IGNES, one in two homes in France is effectively a heat trap.
Among 1,750 users of the classified ads platform Leboncoin surveyed in June, eight out of 10 said they had experienced discomfort during periods of extreme heat, with a third saying they would consider moving if heatwaves became more intense.
Experts have warned that due to climate change, this is to be expected.
France's national weather agency said on Monday that as France braced for its fifth heatwave of the season, "future summers will generally be hotter than those experienced to date".
For Leboncoin's marketing director Sophie Bourg, heatwaves are now "firmly recognised as a structural factor in housing choices" in France.
"Coolness and summer comfort have become a property criterion in their own right."
Orientation, floor level, swimming pools, air conditioning, shutters, the ability to create through-draughts, outdoor space, shaded terraces and even the presence of trees in a neighbourhood are now among the issues increasingly raised by buyers or tenants.
"Buyers are no longer looking only at the property itself, but at how liveable it is," said Yann Jehanno, president of the Laforet estate agency network.
"They are asking estate agents very practical questions about temperatures during the last heatwave, whether it is possible to ventilate the home at night and whether people sleep well in the bedrooms."
The concern is already affecting the appeal of certain properties.
Christian Tokoto, an estate agent with Guy Hoquet Paris 5 Maubert, is trying to sell "a magnificent apartment with large windows" in Paris's well-heeled fifth district.
"Despite lots of viewings, clients tell us it's 'too hot' because it doesn't have windows on both sides. So for now it's still on the market."
Air conditioning, long disdained in France, is "no longer taboo at all", Jehanno said.
It is "a huge selling point for many buyers" if it is already installed, especially in blocks where getting permission for an air conditioning unit can be complicated, said Laetitia Caron, chief executive of real estate media company PAP.
Sellers have adapted accordingly, she added, placing greater emphasis in listings on features linked to summer comfort such as air conditioning and shutters.
The impact of recent heatwaves on where people choose to live is harder to assess.
"We are not seeing an exodus yet," Bourg said.
But whereas people once chose a location primarily for its attractiveness and the opportunities it offered, they are now also making decisions based on "climatic comfort", something she describes as entirely new.
Jehanno believes these trends reflect a lasting change in attitudes.
There is "clearly an impact from climate change on the property market", he said, pointing to challenges such as heatwaves, wildfires and other weather extremes.
Such risks, he said, make it increasingly difficult for buyers "to plan ahead over the 10 to 20 years of a mortgage".
The writers are from AFP

Title: Taliban govt building diplomacy despite lack of recognition
Article:
FIVE years after returning to power, Afghanistan's Taliban authorities have built working relationships with a slate of countries, despite a lack of formal recognition.
Russia remains the only nation to officially recognise the Taliban government.
Many Western countries have demanded to see domestic reforms on human rights before considering doing the same.
But many states are nevertheless engaging with Afghanistan's leaders, including Britain and European Union members, driven largely by practical considerations.
Beyond the high walls of the Foreign Ministry in central Kabul stand embassies, rows of travel agencies and an airline billboard promising: "We're all connected."
While few Afghans have the means to go abroad, their government "seeks relations with all countries", according to Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid.
The authorities' diplomatic strategy has involved hosting envoys in Kabul — and frequently publishing the photos — including those from China, Japan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Britain.
"Countries of the region and our neighbouring states have particular importance because our economic ties and interests are closely linked," Mujahid said last month.
This year, officials from Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan gathered in Kabul, as landlocked Central Asia seeks trade routes through Afghanistan to access the sea beyond.
Erica Gaston, who was part of a team mandated by the United Nations Security Council to identify strategies for addressing the challenges in Afghanistan, said regional nations were "always more pragmatic" in dealing with the Taliban authorities.
"You had much more receptivity among regional member states to say, 'this is the reality that we have in our region and engagement is inevitable'," said Gaston, who heads the Conflict Prevention and Sustaining Peace Programme at the UN University Centre for Policy Research.
But foreign funds have been scarce as investors remain wary of the Taliban government's limited official recognition, with rumours that Iran would follow Russia falling flat.
Despite this, many Taliban officials travel abroad, including a delegation that flew to Brussels in June for talks with 15 EU nations about returning failed asylum-seekers to Afghanistan.
A spokesperson for the bloc said: "Those who have no legal right to stay in Europe must be returned."
Germany has been at the forefront and deported an Afghan not convicted of any crime for the first time since the Taliban's 2021 return to power, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said in July.
For Gaston, the passage of time has meant "more and more countries accept that this is the reality, even if it's a reality that they don't like or condone".
But many have restricted further ties until they see changes in Afghanistan, particularly on rules that stop girls' education at age 12. Yet no policy shift is expected.
Accusing Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and chief justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani of crimes against humanity over the persecution of women and girls, the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for them last year.
Afghan women remain banned from a host of places, including UN premises.
A UN source in Kabul said the ability to exert influence on the authorities remains "highly issue-dependent".
"Some of these issues are kind of fairly impenetrable, but then you have other issues on which you are able to make progress," the source said, citing positive relations in some parts of Afghanistan on counternarcotics and humanitarian access.
Multiple nations stepped in this year when Afghanistan and Pakistan went to war, with China hosting talks after hundreds of civilians were killed.
Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Iran, Turkiye, Uzbekistan and Malaysia were also engaged in trying to stop the fighting.
India has strengthened its ties with the Taliban government. In June, India's UN envoy suggested a rethink was necessary on sanctions — a travel ban, asset freeze and arms embargo — that target dozens of Taliban members.
"The political reality of Afghan-istan has changed in the last five years. The current UN sanctions regime must take that into account," said Harish Parvathaneni.
The UN source said engagement with the Afghan government is "the current state of play".
"Everybody recognises the fact that, essentially, Afghanistan is fully controlled by the de facto (Taliban) authorities and, essentially, there are multiple issues on which the world, the region, has to deal with them," the source said.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: 5 BNM warnings, yet no action by Tabung Haji
Article:
