THE revelation that Bank Negara Malaysia  issued five warnings to Tabung Haji between 2014 and 2017 over its financial position raises a fundamental question: How was the warning from the country's central bank allowed to be repeatedly ignored? Five warnings cannot be dismissed as oversight.
The repeated nature of the warnings suggests that the concerns were known over a prolonged period.
Who was responsible to act on the warnings? The central question is not just whether Bank Negara had warned Tabung Haji, but who received the warnings, what actions were demanded, who decided against acting against the warnings and were these decisions reported to the board or the responsible ministry?
Where was the board? A board exists to provide oversight and challenge the management. Did the fund's governance structure give the board sufficient independence and authority?
Tabung Haji, being a statutory body, is governed by the Tabung Haji Act 1995, meaning the board's statutory powers, duties and governance are regulated by the act.
Following the disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, the Finance Ministry had reiterated that Tabung Haji's board of directors and management have the primary responsibility for determining its direction and managing its operations.
But it has subsidiaries and associate companies that are governed by the Companies Act 2026, which imposes significant legal duties on directors. The RCI report did point to political interference in Tabung Haji's management and profit distribution.
Did such interference affect the board's and management's decision-making powers, causing the financial distress to spiral into a crisis? Institutions entrusted with people's life savings cannot operate on the basis of hoping that financial problems will eventually resolve themselves.
Were depositors given an accurate picture? This is particularly important because Tabung Haji continued to make profit distributions despite its liabilities exceeding its assets.
No management or board of any substance could have missed these signals. The issue is not merely poor investment performance, but whether financial reporting and public communication gave a misleading impression of the institution's health.
Why did it take a crisis to trigger action? The eventual restructuring and government action may have stabilised the fund, but the bigger lesson is that rescue is never a good substitute for prevention.
Early warnings are useful only if institutions are compelled to respond to them. The reforms must address this precise failure. The proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act, including clearer accounting requirements, penalties for misreporting and greater Securities Commission oversight of investments, are welcome.
But the effectiveness of these reforms will depend on whether there are clear lines of responsibility and consequences when warnings are ignored.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 447 red-tape reform projects generate RM2.95bil in compliance savings
Article:
KUCHING: A total of 447 projects under the federal government's Bureaucratic Red-Tape Reform (RKB) initiative have been implemented to date, generating an estimated RM2.95 billion in compliance-cost savings.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said the savings were calculated using a compliance-cost formula developed by the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC), reported Borneo Post.
He said another 500 RKB projects were planned for next year, with the government targeting RM2.5 billion in savings.
"For next year, we will undertake another 500 bureaucratic reform projects and we are targeting RM2.5 billion in savings," he told reporters after the Sarawak Integrity Day (HIS) 2026 celebration at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) here today.
Shamsul Azri said the RKB framework was part of the government's wider public service reform efforts to improve efficiency.
He said progress was also reflected in Malaysia's performance in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking, with the country climbing from 34th in 2024 to 23rd in 2025 and 15th among 70 economies this year.
Malaysia was also ranked second in Asean behind Singapore.
"One of the contributors to this position is government efficiency," he said.
Shamsul Azri said Malaysia's government efficiency ranking improved from 25th to 14th, while business efficiency rose from 32nd to 16th.
The country was also ranked sixth globally in the bureaucracy indicator.
Earlier in his speech, Shamsul Azri said efforts to improve efficiency must be underpinned by integrity, accountability and trust.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Colombia declares three days mourning for quake victims
Article:
BOGOTA: Colombia on Wednesday declared three days of mourning for victims of an earthquake that demolished buildings in the west of the country, killing more than 200 people.
At 7.4 magnitude, Monday's quake was the strongest to hit Colombia this century.
The government said flags would be lowered to half-staff on official buildings, as well as at Colombian embassies around the world, "in honor of all the dead."
Frantic attempts to find survivors continued, as authorities revised the death toll down to 216 after local officials in Cali corrected earlier figures.
In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.
The first two days after an earthquake are crucial for finding survivors under rubble, with some experts saying there is a 72-hour window, after which hopes quickly tail off.
There was joy on Tuesday when rescuers pulled out 32-year-old Daniela Largo.
"We were losing hope and then we received a call," said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.
Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.
From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.
Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.
The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia's largest disaster responses in years.
Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.
One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.
"We lost everything, but we're alive," said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.
In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.
Many Colombians mobilized to help.
Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.
"It's about wanting to help your community, your city and your country," said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.
President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.
The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops hunt loan shark over paint attacks on dead man's family
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: Police are investigating after a business premises in Kampung Baru Sungai Buloh here was splashed with yellow paint and a notice claiming an outstanding loan involving the owner's late son was pasted on its roller shutter.
Sungai Buloh district police chief Superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said police received a report on Aug 6 after the complainant discovered the damage.
He said the incident was believed to have occurred at 7.50am on Aug 5.
"The notice contained a claim regarding a loan debt involving the complainant's late son," he said in a statement.
Hafiz said the complainant also received a WhatsApp message from an unidentified number containing a video of the paint-splashing incident and photographs of the notice.
"Initial investigations found that the incident was believed to have been carried out by an unidentified man.
"The complainant was unaware whether his late son had ever obtained a loan from any unlicensed moneylender," he said.
Police are tracing and identifying the suspect.
The case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for causing mischief, which carries a jail term of between 1 and 5 years, or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
The incident comes amid claims by MCA Public Services and Complaints Department head Datuk Seri Michael Chong that the family
had been repeatedly harassed
by suspected illegal moneylenders following the death of their 35-year-old son, Chew, on July 1.
Chong said the family's machinery shop was first splashed with yellow paint on Aug 5, followed by brown paint the next day, while red paint was later thrown at a customer's car on Aug 8.
He described the sequence as a "traffic light" warning system allegedly used by moneylenders. The family was also allegedly contacted over an outstanding RM28,000 debt linked to Chew.
Chong said the alleged debt comprised RM10,000 in principal, RM3,000 in interest and RM15,000 in so-called "paint fees". The family was later offered a RM25,000 settlement.
Chew's mother, identified only as Lai, said the family had no knowledge of any financial problems involving her son, whom she described as quiet and filial.
Chong said the alleged moneylenders also contacted Chew's wife through WeChat and demanded payment despite being informed of his death.
He said CCTV footage of the subsequent paint attacks had been handed to police.
His department has received 226 complaints involving illegal moneylending, with debts totalling more than RM21 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Uncle, 8-year-old nephew die in Klang shoplot blaze
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Two people died while two others were rescued after a fire broke out at a three-storey shoplot in Taman Bayu Perdana, Klang, this evening.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.51pm before personnel from the Port Klang Fire and Rescue Station arrived eight minutes later.
He said firefighters found the blaze on the second floor of a Class A building, with about 90 per cent of the premises damaged.
"Based on information from the family, there were four people in the building, two of whom were rescued by members of the public.
"After the fire was extinguished, two other victims who were trapped were found in separate toilets at 6.33pm," he said in a statement today.
The victims were a 66-year-old man and an eight-year-old boy, who were believed to have died in the toilets.
Ashrul Riezal said Health Ministry personnel confirmed the deaths before the bodies were handed over to the police Forensics Unit at 10.15pm.
"The two victims were uncle and nephew.
"The two survivors suffered breathing difficulties and were taken to Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR), Klang, for treatment," he said.
He said the department's forensic team, together with its K9 unit, conducted preliminary investigations to determine the cause of the fire.
"The premises have been handed over to the department's Fire Investigation Unit for further action. Firefighting operations ended completely at 10.05pm," he said.
Meanwhile, South Klang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey confirmed the incident and said an official statement would be issued soon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: When neutrality pays: How Malaysia is navigating the global fuel crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — With no end in sight, the war between the United States and Iran has left countries scrambling to shore up their fuel supplies and secure alternative sources of energy.
The Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route carrying about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows, has remained severely disrupted since the conflict erupted in late February.
Almost 40 per cent of Malaysia’s crude oil imports pass through the waterway, making any prolonged disruption a significant concern for the country’s energy security.
Malaysia, a net importer of crude oil, produces about 350,000 barrels of oil a day but consumes about 700,000 barrels, according to the Finance Ministry.
Malaysia also subsidises fuel for domestic consumption, keeping pump prices below those in some major oil-producing countries such as Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Fuel subsidy spending surged from nearly RM800 million a month in January and February to around RM5 billion a month in March and April after global oil prices spiked following the outbreak of the war.
If high global oil prices persist, the country could face an overall fuel subsidy bill of about RM40 billion by the end of 2026.
Despite the pressure, Malaysia is turning the energy crunch into an opportunity to strengthen its diplomatic relationships, leveraging its long-held policy of neutrality and non-alignment.
Three developments illustrate how.
First, safe passage for Malaysian vessels through Hormuz
Malaysia maintains diplomatic relations with Iran despite their different political and sectarian orientations, while continuing to engage with Tehran through diplomatic channels.
On March 1, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim condemned the Israeli and US strikes against Iran, including the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as “barbaric and illegal” and urged for an immediate ceasefire.
Those diplomatic ties proved useful when the energy crisis hit home.
Iran subsequently cleared seven Malaysian-owned vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz for free due to Malaysia being a ‘friendly nation’, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Bernama on March 31, citing Iran’s Ambassador to Malaysia Valiollah Mohammadi.
Malaysia again benefited from its diplomatic ties when a Petronas vessel sailing from Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, was cleared to transit the Red Sea in July, after the Iran-backed Houthis threatened to restrict passage through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Anwar confirmed this on July 25 and said the Petronas-owned ship is slated to arrive in Melaka this month.
Second, securing longer-term supplies from friendly partners
Malaysia currently has sufficient fuel supplies and is working to secure longer-term stocks as the global energy crisis continues.
In doing so, the country is leveraging its broad diplomatic relationships with Russia and Central Asian countries to explore new energy sources and supply arrangements.
During Anwar’s maiden visit to Turkmenistan in June, national oil company Petronas secured rights to operate Blocks 9 and 10 in one of the country’s major gas-producing areas.
Petronas is expected to begin exploratory drilling there in December.
That same month, Russia pledged to provide Malaysia with long-term supplies of petrol, diesel and gas for at least 20 years, with the arrangement being finalised between the two countries.
The development comes as Malaysia continues its policy of non-alignment and has not joined Western sanctions against Russia over its invasion of Ukraine.
Third, using energy security to strengthen regional ties
Even as it navigates the energy crunch, Malaysia continues to maintain energy supply relationships with partners that are also seeking greater security amid global market uncertainty.
In June, Anwar announced that Petronas would supply up to two million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) a year to Japan’s largest power generation company, Jera, over a 20-year period starting in 2028.
Prior to that, he told his Australian counterpart Anthony Albanese in April that Malaysia would prioritise selling fuel surplus to Australia.
Anwar also said in June that Malaysia’s diesel surplus could be used to assist countries in need, including Timor-Leste, which became Asean’s 11th member last year.
Taken together, the developments underscore how Malaysia’s non-aligned foreign policy has given it room to maintain relationships across geopolitical divides while securing energy supplies and supporting regional partners during a period of heightened uncertainty.

Title: Tabung Haji RCI report to go to police, MACC, Bank Negara, IRB for full investigation, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will go to the relevant authorities for a full investigation based on all findings and information contained in the report, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the authorities included the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), agencies responsible for matters under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act (AMLA), Bank Negara Malaysia and the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
“As a start, we will hand it over to the authorities as announced by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim), whether the PDRM, MACC, AMLA, Bank Negara or IRB, to conduct a full investigation based on all the findings.
“This includes information contained in the report, as well as additional information provided by Finance Minister II (Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan) and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Tabung Haji RCI report, yesterday.”
He said this to reporters after attending the Handover of Sponsorship Contributions for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations here today.
The TH RCI report was made public on July 29. It documented various management and operational weaknesses at TH between 2014 and 2020 and made 25 recommendations for improvement, 75 per cent of which had been implemented by TH as of July 30 this year.
Asked about calls by Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pakatan Harapan (PH) lawmakers for the government to establish a new TH RCI covering the 2021-2025 period, Fahmi, who is also Madani Government spokesman, said it would need the Cabinet and the King to decide.
“We all know that the decision to have the RCI was not only a Cabinet decision. As it is a Royal Commission of Inquiry, it also required the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong,” he said.
Meanwhile, Fahmi described the attendance of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) MPs at yesterday’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting to debate the TH RCI report as a wise and appropriate move.
He said this contrasted with other opposition parties in Perikatan Nasional (PN), which did not attend the debate.
“We must remember that this RCI was established in 2021 when PAS members and the Leader of the Opposition (Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin) were members of the Cabinet.
“But what I regret is that they did not attend the debate at all. They have missed a good opportunity.
“Perhaps...I am not sure, they were there when the RCI was initiated and when it completed its work, but they refused to attend the debate. What are they running away from?” he said.
Thirty-nine MPs debated the RCI report after Zulkifli presented his ministerial briefing on the matter at the special Dewan Rakyat sitting yesterday.
Some opposition MPs, however, staged a walkout from the Dewan Rakyat and boycotted the ministerial briefing and debate sessions after objecting to Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul’s decision to proceed without the presence of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. — Bernama

Title: Two accused flee Kulim court, one slides down pillar to escape police
Article:
KULIM, Aug 12 — Two men attending a case mention at the Kulim Magistrate’s Court here today fled the court compound after spotting police officers waiting to re-arrest them in connection with another case.
Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the incident occurred at about 10am after both accused, aged 27 and 31, had completed their case mention and document submission.
He said both men were facing charges under Sections 324 and 353 of the Penal Code and had been granted bail pending trial after being charged at the same court on April 30.
“The first accused was granted bail of RM4,000 while the second was granted RM3,000. The case was fixed for re-mention on June 8, July 12 and today for document submission and case management,” he said in a statement today.
Syamsul said after completing the court proceedings, both men exited through the rear door before spotting police officers from the Seberang Perai Selatan (SPS) District Police Headquarters at the front entrance, who were there to re-arrest them in connection with another case.
“One of them immediately fled within the court compound and slid down a pillar from the first floor, while the other re-entered the building before escaping through the rear route.
“Both subsequently escaped by climbing over the rear fence,” he said, adding that police were working to locate the two men.
Earlier, a 24-second video went viral showing chaotic scenes at the Kulim Court Complex, in which a man believed to be one of the accused was seen climbing over a fence before fleeing. — Bernama

Title: Rubbish lorry crashes through Pantai Hillpark condo wall, crushes three cars
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — A rubbish lorry believed to have suffered brake failure lost control and crashed into a condominium boundary wall, crushing three cars at Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the lorry was travelling downhill along a straight, sloping road when the incident occurred at about 4.10am.
He said the lorry veered off the road after its brakes failed, before coming down on three cars parked in the area.
The lorry driver, a 41-year-old local man, suffered an injury to his left leg, he said.
“The Kuala Lumpur JSPT immediately began efforts to locate the lorry driver after receiving the report, as he was not at the scene. He was successfully located while receiving treatment at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, HUKM,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Zamzuri said two Bangladeshi workers, both around 25, were carrying out rubbish collection work in the area when the incident occurred, but neither was injured as they were on the road at the time.
He said the lorry driver presented himself at the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Police Station at 3.15pm today to lodge a report on the incident.
“A breathalyser test found no alcohol in the driver’s system. The lorry will be sent to Puspakom for further examination to determine the exact cause of the incident,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless and inconsiderate driving. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry: Prices of non subsidised RON97, RON95, diesel cheaper by 20, 15 and 10 sen respectively from Aug 13 to 19
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — The retail prices of non subsidised petroleum products for the period from August 13 to August 19, 2026, sees a drop, with RON97 down by 20 sen per liter, unsubsidised RON95 dropping by 15 sen, and unsubsidised diesel dropping by 10 sen.
According to a statement by the Ministry of Finance (MoF), for the stated period, the price of RON97 is set at RM4.15 per litre compared to RM4.35 previously, while unsubsidised RON95 is priced at RM3.62 per litre  compared to RM3.77, and unsubsidised diesel is set at RM4.47 per litre compared to RM4.57 previously.
At the same time, subsidised petroleum prices remain unchanged at RM1.99 per litre for RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and RM2.10 per litre for diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel).
MoF stated that the Madani Government shoulders a subsidy of RM1.63 per litre for eligible users under Budi95, equivalent to about 82 per cent of the RM1.99 per litre price paid at the pump while for Budi Diesel, a subsidy of RM2.37 per litre is borne, equivalent to about 113 per cent of the RM2.10 per litre price paid at the pump.
Prices for the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control Systems (SKDS) remain at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre , respectively.
In the meantime, MoF noted that the price drop follows the fall in global oil prices last week, when hopes for a resolution to the conflict between the United States and Iran caused global oil prices to trade at lower levels for most of the week.
Brent crude oil prices also dropped below US$80 (RM330) a barrel at the beginning of the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) price calculation period, marking the lowest level in three weeks.
“However, geopolitical risk premiums rose again toward the end of the APM calculation period as prospects for negotiations between the United States and Iran deteriorated following new demands put forward by both parties,” according to the statement.
The ministry said Brent prices rose by nearly five per cent on Monday as concerns over the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz peaked again.
“Uncertainty regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continues to pose risks of global oil supply disruptions, thereby placing pressure on petroleum prices. Consequently, petroleum product prices are expected to continue experiencing significant fluctuations in the near future,” according to MoF. — Bernama

Title: Singapore fugitive flees to Johor, ends up kidnapped for S$80,000 ransom
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 12 — A 32-year-old Singaporean wanted man, who fled to Johor for refuge, was instead kidnapped and assaulted before his family was blackmailed with a S$80,000 (about RM255,400) ransom.
Federal Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the victim, who is wanted by the Singapore police, had initially entered the country illegally at the end of May.
He said the victim was met by one of the six suspects in Johor Bahru shortly before his 28-year-old girlfriend also entered the country illegally.
“While the victim was in the midst of asking for assistance, he and his girlfriend were then kidnapped by the suspect.
“The suspects also forcefully took the victim’s cash consisting of S$12,000 and RM41,400.
“They then hatched a plan and demanded a S$80,000 ransom from the victim’s mother in Singapore,” he told reporters at the Johor police contingent headquarters here today.
Also present was Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad and senior officers.
Following the ransom demand, Kumar said the victim’s mother then reported the matter to the Singapore Police Force (SPF) before investigators reached out to their Malaysian counterparts.
He said a Bukit Aman and Johor state CID task force was assembled to catch the suspects.
“While being detained, the male victim was deliberately slashed on both thighs before a photo of him was sent to his mother as a reminder of the ransom amount.
“As a result of negotiations, the male victim’s family and the suspect then agreed to a ransom sum of S$25,000, where S$5,000 was paid in advance online,” he said, adding that the remainder of the ransom was to be paid in cash during a meeting between the suspect and the victim’s family here.
Kumar said police then arrested a 40-year-old suspect during the ransom exchange held at a supermarket in Nusa Bestari, Iskandar Puteri at 6pm yesterday.
He said police also managed to rescue and free the two victims.
“Following that, police conducted a series of raids in Skudai and managed to arrest four men and a local woman, aged between 30 and 46, who are believed to be behind the kidnapping,” he said.
Checks showed that five of the six suspects had previous records involving criminal and drug offences. Four suspects also tested positive for methamphetamine abuse.
Kumar said police managed to recover the Singaporean and Malaysian currencies from the suspects that are believed to belong to the victim.
“This is in addition to house keys, mobile phones, jewellery, a Rolex watch and a Perodua Axia car with a total value of RM264,440.
“The motive for the kidnapping is still under investigation and police are actively tracking down other suspects who are still at large,” he said.
Kumar said the male victim was supposed to be under parole in Singapore, but fled and entered Johor illegally.
He said police believed that the victim’s contacts here had taken advantage of his situation to blackmail him.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, which is kidnapping for ransom.
The suspects have been remanded for 10 days starting today, while the two victims were also anrrested for illegally entering Malaysia.

Title: Five Chinese nationals arrested in Sri Petaling, Pudu over housebreakings in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Five Chinese nationals suspected to have been involved in several housebreaking incidents in the capital were arrested in two separate raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu here on Sunday.
Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said investigations revealed that the suspects may have been involved in a housebreaking incident in Taman Desa Petaling on August 4, which caused the victim to suffer losses of about RM6,000 involving cash, jewelry, and a luxury-branded sling bag.
“During the raid at approximately 9.30pm, the police also seized a vehicle along with various tools used for housebreaking,” he said in a statement today.
Fadil said the police also recovered items belonging to the victim alongside various other luxury items including watches, wallets, and cash in various foreign currencies totalling more than RM10,000.
According to him, the suspects, aged between 38 and 58, are also believed to be involved in two other housebreaking cases around the Cheras area.
He said all suspects were remanded for four days starting Monday until tomorrow to assist with investigations under Section 457 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Kedah woman pleads guilty to organising RM1.7m kootu fund scheme
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 12 — A woman pleaded guilty at the Sessions Court here today to organising a kootu fund scheme, resulting in estimated losses of more than RM1.7 million between July last year and July this year.
Siti Zulaika Ahmad Sabri, 36, entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Sharmila Abdul Samad.
According to the charge, Siti Zulaika allegedly organised a kootu fund involving 52 participants aged between 24 and 62, with each participant required to contribute cash to the scheme in Kampung Padang Satu, Bukit Kayu Hitam, Changlun.
She was charged under Section 3 of the Kootu Funds (Prohibition) Act 1971 (Act 28), which provides for a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to 10 years, or both upon conviction.
The court denied bail and fixed September 22 for the facts of the case to be presented and for sentencing. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan state assembly passes Syariah Criminal Offences Bill 2026
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Kelantan state legislative assembly today passed the Syariah Criminal Offences (Kelantan) Bill 2026 to streamline and strengthen its provisions, making them more systematic, clear and authoritative.
The Bill was tabled by Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan and debated by six state assemblymen from Pasir Tumboh, Melor, Galas, Jelawat, Kota Lama and Chempaka.
The winding-up speech was delivered by Mohamed Fadzli and Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud before the Bill was read for the second and third time and subsequently passed unanimously in the presence of Kelantan state assembly Speaker Datuk Mohd Amar Nik Abdullah.
Earlier, Mohd Nassuruddin said the Bill was not drafted without careful planning. It is a legislation that had been meticulously enhanced and gone through various stages before being tabled in the assembly.
“The strength of this Bill lies in its revitalisation based on maqasid syariah (wisdom behind Islamic rulings), with each provision on offences carefully structured to ensure that every aspect of the legislation is aligned with the objectives of Islamic law.
“This approach is not something foreign as it is the underlying spirit that already exists in the Kelantan Syariah Criminal Code (I) Enactment 2019,” he said during the Kelantan state assembly sitting today.
The Bill comprises nine parts, 62 clauses and one schedule, with several reforms, including provisions relating to the obligation of performing obligatory prayers, safeguarding the private parts and bodily organs, safeguarding the intellect, restorative punishment, prioritising whipping as a punishment, and a compound mechanism.
On February 9, 2024, the Federal Court, in an 8-1 majority decision, declared 16 of the 18 provisions in the Kelantan Syariah Criminal Code (I) Enactment 2019 null and void, ruling that the state legislative assembly did not have the power to legislate offences falling under Federal jurisdiction.
The decision followed a petition filed by a lawyer from Kelantan, sparking debate on the division of powers between the Federal and state governments in legislating Syariah criminal offences. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak closes 108 schools in Serian division as API readings exceed 200
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 12 — A total of 108 schools in the Serian Division have been temporarily closed after Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the area exceeded 200, reaching the very unhealthy range.
Announcing the move, Sarawak Deputy Premier and State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the closure was a preventive measure to safeguard the health and well-being of students and school personnel.
“Teaching and Learning from Home (PdPR) will continue throughout the closure period to ensure that students’ learning continuity is not disrupted,” he said in a statement.
Under the National Haze Action Plan, schools, kindergartens and nurseries are to be closed when API readings reach 200, subject to the jurisdiction of the Sarawak State Education Department director.
As of 4pm today, Serian recorded an API reading of 202, while Tebedu recorded 212, placing both areas in the very unhealthy category.
Another 11 areas — Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Sarikei, Sibu, Bintulu, Samalaju, Miri, Lundu, Lubok Antu and Lawas — recorded unhealthy API readings ranging from 101 to 200.
Mukah, Kapit, ILP Miri, Limbang and Bario remained in the moderate category, while no area in Sarawak recorded good or hazardous air quality.
Uggah said air quality in Sarawak had shown an upward trend in API readings since Aug 1.
Citing data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC), he said 75 hotspots were detected in Sarawak between Aug 1 and 11, compared with 3,853 hotspots detected in Kalimantan, Indonesia, during the same period.
He said the prevailing South-west Monsoon, which began on May 14 and is expected to continue until September, could contribute to transboundary haze and deteriorating air quality in Sarawak.
“Sarawak is likely to continue experiencing haze over the next few days if biomass burning increases outside Sarawak’s borders,” he said.
Uggah said SDMC and relevant agencies would continue monitoring air quality, weather conditions, hotspots and fire incidents throughout the state.
The public, particularly children, the elderly, pregnant women and those with respiratory or heart conditions, are advised to minimise outdoor activities when air quality reaches unhealthy levels or above.
Meanwhile, the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) reminded the public against open burning, warning that offenders could face a fine of up to RM100,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
The public is also urged to help extinguish small fires and report open-burning cases to the nearest NREB office or its hotlines at 082-447488 or 082-319500. — The Borneo Post

Title: KLIA CCTV monitoring to be improved to address blind spots, says home minister
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) will improve the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) if there are blind spots.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said there are currently 5,000 CCTVs at KLIA Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, but the monitoring aspect of the system also needs attention.
“The issue is not CCTV. If there are blind spots, we will improve that,” he told reporters after visiting the family of the late Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, who died, believed to have been electrocuted in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday, at his family home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh here today.
He said AKPS is currently in the second phase of operations which involves several forms of procurement, including CCTV as part of the equipment and infrastructure requirements.
“Just equipment, infra. But we also need to look at the people who supervise or monitor the infra themselves in terms of their training standards and so on,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar thanks Brunei Sultan for prayers, concern after surgery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today received a phone call from Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei Darussalam, who enquired about his health and prayed for his well-being.
In a Facebook post, Anwar expressed his appreciation for the Sultan’s prayers and concern.
“I also pray that His Majesty will always be blessed with good health and remain under the protection and mercy of Allah SWT,” he said.
Anwar also said he would have an audience with Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah in Bandar Seri Begawan next week in conjunction with the 27th Annual Leaders’ Consultation (ALC) between Malaysia and Brunei.
Last Monday, Anwar underwent an elective laparoscopic procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia and remains under close monitoring by a team of medical specialists. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Thailand step up cooperation on border security, cross-border crime
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Thailand are strengthening border security cooperation through government-to-government (G2G) and police-to-police (P2P) platforms, including addressing cross-border crime threats.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that the G2G cooperation is implemented through the Malaysia-Thailand Border Security Management Committee, which meets twice a year.
He said that the P2P cooperation involves the states bordering Thailand, namely Perlis, Kedah and Kelantan, to ensure that security aspects are always given attention.
“This police cooperation usually involves three things: intelligence sharing, capacity building, and joint operations, if necessary,” he said.
He said this to reporters after visiting the family of the late Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim at his family’s home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh here today. Mohamad Nur Hafiz was believed to have died from an electric shock in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday.
Saifuddin Nasution also said that border security issues were also discussed in the recent official meeting with his Thai counterpart, including during the visit of Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul to Malaysia.
“The management of this border area is very sensitive because it involves the sovereignty of two countries, the movement of people, and elements of cross-border crime. All of them are on our radar.
“We do not resolve it through back-and-forth media statements, but rather through appropriate platforms and forums in an orderly manner as neighbouring countries,” he added. — Bernama

Title: IPTS student charged with murder after alleged drunk-driving incident in Kuala Langat
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 12 — A student of a private higher education institution (IPTS) who went viral after allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol was charged in the Telok Datok Magistrates’ Court in Kuala Langat today with murdering an elderly man last week.
N. Vishwesh, 23, nodded in understanding when the charge was read out before Magistrate Maslinda Selamat, but no plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
According to the charge, the man is accused of murdering Eng Kim Kheng @ Ng Kim Swee, 78, at Kilometre 38, Jalan Klang-Banting-Port Dickson, in the Kuala Langat district at about 7.20pm on August 7.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, whipping of not less than 12 strokes upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Amirul Syafiq Yazid appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by T. Mishant.
The court did not grant bail to the accused and fixed October 1 for mention.
Previously, a video recording of an accident at the Kanchong Bengkok traffic light intersection in Banting went viral, showing a man admitting to driving under the influence of alcohol while another man was seen lying on the road with a leg injury. — Bernama

Title: Fresh RCI into Tabung Haji’s 2021-2025 performance needs Agong’s consent, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Any decision to form a fresh Royal Commission of Inquiry to scrutinise Lembaga Tabung Haji’s performance from 2021 to 2025 will need the Agong’s consent first, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
The Anwar government tabled the report of the inquiry’s findings in a special Parliamentary sitting for debate yesterday, more than three years after the report was published.
TH lost billions from poor investments, the inquiry found, prompting the authorities to crack down on those named in the report.
After the debates, several Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pakatan Harapan (PH) MPs suggested that the period should be subjected to assessment as well, as the existing investigation only covers 2014 to 2020.
“There are two decisions that need to be made. First, at the Cabinet level, on whether to proceed with or expand (the investigation), because we know that when the RCI was established in 2021, it did not involve the Cabinet alone,” he told reporters after officiating the Sponsorship Handover Ceremony for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day Celebration here.
“In fact, because it is a Royal Commission of Inquiry, the decision also requires the consent of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.”
Police have recorded statements from 134 witnesses, including 10 recently called in, as part of investigations into the RCI’s findings, according to news reports.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa was reported saying around 10 witnesses had previously given statements, including individuals linked to TH’s management and organisational structure.
Fahmi said for now, government will leave it to the authorities to conduct full investigations based on the findings and information contained in the report.
Investigations would also be based on the additional information provided by Finance Minister II, Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Zulkifli Hasan, during the winding-up speech on the debate over the TH RCI report.
Amir told Parliament this morning seven of the 14 troubled investments of TH resulted in “total losses”, with the collective losses totaling some RM13 billion.

Title: Fadhlina: Character education is more than teaching youths to be ‘good’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Character education should encourage young people to voice their views, think critically and remain respectful when faced with differing opinions, Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said.
In a Facebook post today, Fadhlina said that at the National Madani Youth Forum, she observed young people learning to articulate their thoughts, express their positions, consider differing views and defend their arguments.
“This is the character education we want to foster. It is not merely about teaching children to be good. We want them to speak up confidently, think critically and remain respectful when opinions differ,” she said.
She said character education must move in tandem with efforts to promote the Malay language, including by creating more spaces for young people to use it.
She said the Malay language would be strengthened when the next generation saw it as a language capable of expressing their thoughts.
“Our job is not to determine what they should say, but to ensure that when they speak, they have the knowledge to put forward their arguments and the courtesy to listen.
“A mature nation is not one where everyone agrees. It is one built by a generation that understands how to disagree,” Fadhlina said. — Bernama

Title: Socso incentive claims land four Melaka company directors in court
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 12 — Four company directors pleaded not guilty in the Ayer Keroh Sessions Court here today to charges of submitting claim documents containing false information to agents of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) to deceive the agency two years ago.
The company directors were accused of providing two Perkeso agents with documents, namely the Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Verification Form under the company's name containing false information, attached in an incentive claim application under the Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Programme.
The first accused, Henry Ratnaike, 45, who is the Director of Alpha Buildcon, faces four charges of committing the offence at Taman Merdeka Jaya, Batu Berendam, in the district of Melaka Tengah on May 10, 2024.
The second accused, Koh Kai Loon, 40, who is the Director of PK Tan Auto and Car Repair, faces one charge of committing the offence at Taman Kasawari Utama, Durian Tunggal, in the state of Melaka on June 14, 2024.
Prima Kerjaya Trading Director Gan Pay Kiat, 32, faces two charges of committing the offence at Jalan KPKs 3, Kompleks Perniagaan Kota Syahbandar on May 27 and 31, 2024.
All three accused were charged with committing offences under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act.
Another director of Alpha Buildcon, Ling Yate May, 58, faces four charges of abetting Henry by providing the Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Verification Form, believed to contain false statements, to Perkeso agents to deceive the agency.
Ling was accused of committing all the offences at Taman Merdeka Jaya, Batu Berendam on May 10, 2024, and was charged under Section 28(1)(c) of the MACC Act 2009 (Act 694), read together with Section 18 of the same Act, which is punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act.
If convicted, all accused face a prison sentence of not more than 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the sum or value of the false or erroneous material particulars if they can be valued or are monetary in nature, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
MACC Deputy Public Prosecutor Sharina Farhana Nor Sa'ari offered bail of RM15,000 for each accused, along with additional conditions requiring all their passports to be surrendered to the court and for them to report to the nearest MACC office once a month until the case is concluded.
Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah granted bail of RM15,000 for Henry, RM9,000 for Koh, RM13,000 for Gan, and RM15,000 for Ling, approved the additional conditions proposed by the prosecution, and set September 14 as the next mention date.
Henry was represented by lawyer FB Ng, while the other three were not represented. — Bernama

Title: Haze worsens in Malaysia as 11 stations record unhealthy API, Serian reaches 204
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 12 — Malaysia has been experiencing haze since August 8, with 11 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and one station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading as of 3pm today, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said.
In a statement today, the ministry said the El Niño phenomenon occurring alongside the Southwest Monsoon had resulted in several areas, particularly southern Peninsular Malaysia and western and southern Sarawak, receiving below-average rainfall.
The combination of lower rainfall and higher temperatures could increase the risk of water shortages, forest and peat fires, as well as haze, particularly in areas experiencing prolonged dry conditions, it said.
As of 3pm today, 11 of the 68 air quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy API readings. These were Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (122), Putrajaya (121), Shah Alam in Selangor (112), and in Sarawak, Miri (152), Samalaju (120), Bintulu (154), Sibu (135), Sarikei (161), Sri Aman (158), Samarahan (177) and Kuching (177).
The Sarawak station at Serian recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 204.
NRES said the deterioration in air quality in Sarawak was caused by transboundary haze as well as local fires at a waste disposal site under the supervision of the Sibu Municipal Council, covering an estimated 1.5 hectares, and forest and bush fires in Sri Aman covering about 100 hectares. Firefighting operations were ongoing at both locations.
Based on the Regional Haze Map and information issued by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) today, dry conditions were observed across southern Asean, except in parts of northern Sumatra where rain was reported.
Isolated hotspots were detected in central and southern Sumatra, as well as southern and eastern Kalimantan, with several hotspots also detected in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Java and Sulawesi.
Moderate smoke plumes were observed in West Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan, while light smoke plumes were observed in southern Sumatra.
Based on NOAA-20 satellite monitoring on Aug 11, 12 hotspots were detected in Malaysia, comprising one in Pahang and 11 in Sarawak. A total of 60 hotspots were detected in Sumatra and 354 in Kalimantan.
Dry weather is expected to continue across most of southern Asean, except northern Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra, where rain is forecast. Prolonged dry conditions could lead to an increase in hotspots and haze, raising the possibility of transboundary haze, NRES said.
At the Asean level, Alert Level 2 was activated on Aug 3. Countries in southern Asean — Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Timor-Leste — are required to submit daily reports and emergency responses on fires, haze and measures taken.
NRES, together with the Department of Environment and Malaysian Meteorological Department, will continue monitoring and reporting developments in the weather, air quality and haze situation.
Relevant ministries, departments and agencies will also implement measures outlined under the National Haze Action Plan and National Open Burning Action Plan based on the alert level.
Members of the public in affected areas are advised to reduce outdoor activities, wear face masks and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.
Open burning is also prohibited to prevent the haze situation from worsening.

Title: Immigration blames airline systems for long-validity passport headaches
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Difficulties experienced by holders of Malaysian International Passports (PMA) with validity periods exceeding 10 years while travelling abroad were caused by systems used by certain airlines, rather than the immigration control systems of foreign countries, according to the Immigration Department.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said that, in terms of border controls and International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards, passports with validity periods exceeding 10 years did not pose a problem.
“It is not the country, it is the airlines. The immigration systems of any country do not have an issue with the validity period because they will simply enter the passport’s validity period.
“From the ICAO perspective and aviation standards, there is no issue... but the airlines have a problem,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Zakaria said the issue involved, among other things, systems used by airlines that set the maximum passport validity period at 10 years.
In this regard, Zakaria said Malaysia would bring the matter to ICAO for coordination with airlines, but no timeframe could be given for resolving the issue as it falls outside the department’s jurisdiction.
He explained that the department was still issuing PMAs with a 10-year validity and had only stopped granting additional validity carried forward from the previous passport that resulted in the overall validity of the new passport exceeding 10 years.
According to him, previously, applicants who renewed their passports early could receive an extension of up to six months based on the remaining validity of their old passports, resulting in the new passport having a validity period of up to 10 years and six months.
“After this, if they renew early, they will no longer get the extra period. They will get 10 years only. It will stop at 10 years,” he said.
Zakaria said existing passport holders whose passports have validity periods exceeding 10 years could obtain replacement passports free of charge.
He said the department would also issue a notice to all airlines to facilitate matters for Malaysians currently travelling abroad.
Regarding the number of 10-year PMAs issued since they were introduced on July 1, Zakaria said about 38,000 passports had been issued so far, of which 26,000 had validity periods exceeding 10 years. — Bernama

Title: Got haze health worries? Ministry steps up monitoring, medical readiness
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Health Ministry (MOH) is strengthening surveillance of haze-related illnesses at health facilities following 10 stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with nine in Sarawak and one in Selangor.
In a statement today, MOH said the preparedness of health facilities, medicine supplies and healthcare personnel had also been stepped up to ensure health services could be provided appropriately should there be an increase in haze-related cases.
According to the ministry, based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) at 9 am yesterday, the nine areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings were Serian, Samarahan, Kuching, Bintulu, Samalaju, Mukah, Sibu, Sarikei and Sri Aman, while the other area was Johan Setia in Selangor.
MOH advised the public, particularly those in affected areas, to reduce physical and strenuous outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100 and to wear an appropriate face mask if they needed to be outdoors.
Educational institutions, government agencies and the private sector were also advised to monitor API readings and adjust outdoor activities according to the air quality level.
“Outdoor sports, co-curricular and strenuous physical activities are advised to be postponed or moved indoors to suitable premises when the API exceeds 100,” the statement said.
The public was also advised to keep windows and doors closed to reduce the entry of polluted air, drink sufficient water and pay special attention to children, the elderly and individuals with chronic illnesses.
MOH also reminded the public not to carry out open burning, which could worsen air quality and increase health risks caused by haze. — Bernama

Title: Kedah PAS vows to continue fight against gambling after Federal Court ruling
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 12 — Kedah PAS today vowed to continue its efforts to eliminate gambling in the state despite the Federal Court dismissing the state government’s bid to appeal a ruling against its ban on issuing and renewing gambling premises licences.
Kedah PAS commissioner Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party accepted the court’s decision but expressed disappointment over the outcome.
“Kedah Pas takes note of the Federal Court’s decision to reject the Kedah government’s application for leave to appeal over the cessation of gambling premises licences.
“We are saddened by the decision, although we respect the court’s ruling,” he said in a statement today.
The Federal Court today dismissed the Kedah government’s application for leave to appeal a ruling declaring its directive not to issue or renew business licences for gambling activities unconstitutional.
A three-member bench led by Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, with Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah and Datuk Azmi Ariffin, unanimously dismissed the application after finding that the questions of law raised did not meet the threshold under Section 96(a) of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964.
Ahmad, who is also Pokok Sena MP, said Kedah PAS considered the state government’s efforts to prevent social ills through the policy justified, but regretted that certain parties had challenged the move.
“How can there still be parties determined to defend the crime of gambling in the state, despite the state government’s efforts to shut down all premises being carried out within the existing legal framework?
“Kedah Pas reiterates that the principle of amar makruf nahi mungkar (enjoining good and forbidding evil) will continue to be upheld in governance,” he said.
The Kedah government previously announced that it would stop issuing licences for gambling premises from Jan 1, 2023, following a decision by the state executive council on Dec 8, 2021.

Title: Court of Appeal says Malaysia is not the right forum for 1MDB suit against UK law firm White & Case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — The Court of Appeal today granted an appeal by UK law firm White & Case LLP against a High Court ruling that allowed a lawsuit filed by 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) on alleged fraud to be heard in Malaysia.
In a unanimous decision, a three-judge panel chaired by Justice Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, sitting with Justices K. Muniandy and Datuk Aliza Sulaiman, ruled that the Kuala Lumpur High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear 1MDB’s suit against the firm.
In delivering the court’s decision, Justice Muniandy said the panel found that the requirements under the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 and the Rules of Court 2012 for the service of proceedings outside Malaysia had not been satisfied.
“The respondent (1MDB) failed to prove that Malaysia is clearly the forum convenient to hear this suit,” he said.
Justice Muniandy added that Patrick Mahony, a director of PetroSaudi International Ltd, is a foreign national residing outside Malaysia and therefore could not serve as a proper “anchor defendant” to justify the service of proceedings out of jurisdiction.
The panel also set aside the High Court’s decision to consolidate 1MDB’s suit against White & Case with a separate suit filed by the sovereign wealth fund against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
“We agree with the appellant that the application for consolidation by the respondent was an unequivocal tactical manoeuvre,” Justice Muniandy said.
The court ordered 1MDB to pay RM130,000 in costs to White & Case.
Meanwhile, 1MDB’s counsel Datuk Lim Chee Wee informed the bench that he had received instructions from his client to seek leave to appeal today’s decision at the Federal Court.
1MDB filed a suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court in 2024, seeking US$1.83 billion and US$33 million in losses from White & Case and Mahony.
The fund alleges that White & Case assisted PetroSaudi in committing fraud and conspired to harm 1MDB while acting as its legal counsel.
The alleged misconduct relates to two corporate transactions: the 2009 joint venture with PetroSaudi International, known as the Good Star phase, and the 2010 restructuring of 1MDB’s stake in the joint venture, which 1MDB claims resulted in significant financial losses.
The writ of summons was served out of jurisdiction on White & Case at their UK offices, and the firm subsequently applied to set aside the service, seeking a declaration that the Malaysian court had no jurisdiction to hear the suit.
Last year, the High Court rejected White & Case’s challenge, ruling that it could hear the lawsuit because the trial witnesses are located in Malaysia. The law firm then appealed this decision to the Court of Appeal.
White & Case is also appealing another High Court decision that ordered this lawsuit to be consolidated with a separate one filed by 1MDB against several other defendants, including Deutsche Bank and PetroSaudi International.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyer Datuk Cyrus Das appeared for the firm. — Bernama

Title: Airport security plan heads to Cabinet next week after Malaysian pilot’s drug bust
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — A plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet next week following the arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia on suspicion of drug smuggling, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the matter was discussed at last week’s Cabinet meeting, which instructed all relevant regulatory agencies to draw up plans to strengthen airport security.
The agencies included the Home Ministry, Transport Ministry, Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Aviation Security, Malaysia Aviation Commission (MAVCOM) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM), he said.
“The agencies met yesterday, and I understand that a paper on the plan to enhance airport security controls will be presented to the Cabinet at next week’s meeting,” he told reporters after visiting the family of the late Cpl Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim in Ketereh here today.
Mohamad Nur Hafiz was believed to have died from an electric shock in Beaufort, Sabah last week.
Saifuddin Nasution said the plan would cover coordination, training, infrastructure and logistics, including the control and operation of scanning machines.
He said airport scanning machines were operated by the AVSEC team in accordance with standards set by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), with emphasis on detecting bombs, sharp weapons and firearms.
“If contraband appears on the screen, it can certainly be detected by the scanning machine. However, the screening procedures do not fall under the routine security checks carried out by the police or AKPS, so we need to realign the procedures,” he said.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had raised the matter with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who had urged all parties involved to give priority to airport security.
He added that the matter was not only about security but also the country’s reputation, particularly as Malaysia had recorded strong tourist arrival figures.
The 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was arrested by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes of drugs. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Saudi Arabia sign pact to share judicial know-how
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Malaysia and Saudi Arabia today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in the judicial field.
The MoU was signed by Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia Azhaniz Teh Azman Teh and Saudi Arabian Minister of Justice Sheikh Dr Waleed Mohammed Alsmani at the Palace of Justice here.
The MoU signing, witnessed by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, was held in conjunction with Sheikh Dr Waleed’s official visit to Malaysia.
According to a statement issued by the Office of the Chief Registrar, the MoU provides a framework for closer cooperation in various areas, including civil case management, judicial technology and digitalisation, the exchange of practical experience and publicly available judicial information, institutional visits and regular exchanges.
It said the MoU marked an important milestone in Malaysia-Saudi Arabia judicial relations by providing a structured platform for closer institutional engagement, knowledge-sharing and continued cooperation towards the efficient administration of justice.
“The Malaysian Judiciary looks forward to the successful implementation of the areas of cooperation set out in the MoU and to further strengthening the longstanding ties between Malaysia and Saudi Arabia,” the statement said.
On the visit, the statement said it reflected the longstanding cordial relations between Malaysia and Saudi Arabia as well as their shared commitment to strengthening judicial cooperation and knowledge-sharing.
The programme also included a courtesy call on Tun Wan Ahmad Farid followed by a judicial dialogue and experience sharing session focusing on Malaysia’s judicial approach to sexual offences against children and the digitalisation of the Judiciary through the e-Court system. — Bernama

Title: RM200,000-plus aid for family of cop killed in Sabah electric shock incident, says home minister
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 12 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will expedite benefits and welfare assistance for the family of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, who died in an electric shock incident in Beaufort, Sabah, last Thursday.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move was aimed at easing the burden on the deceased’s wife, who is raising their two-year-old son.
He said today’s visit to the late officer’s family home, accompanied by Bukit Aman Management director Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat and Sabah deputy police commissioner Datuk Mohd Azhar Hamin, was also a gesture of sympathy from the entire police force.
“We are here to convey the sympathies of the entire police force to the family of the deceased. The loss of any officer, regardless of rank or position, is a great loss to the police force,” he told reporters after visiting the family at their home in Kampung Hutan Pasir, Ketereh, here.
Saifuddin Nasution said the assistance presented included contributions from the Sabah and Kelantan Police Contingents (IPK), as well as takaful payments from the deceased’s contributions as a member of the Police Cooperative, with total contributions and payments exceeding RM200,000.
He said the deceased had named his wife, Fatimah Shahira, as the beneficiary of his monthly pension, while his mother was also named as a pension recipient.
He added that he had instructed the Bukit Aman Management director to expedite other payments due to the family and assured them that the process would not be subjected to the standard procedure.
“I personally assured the wife and family that all matters relating to the process will be expedited and will not go through the standard procedure,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution also said the deceased’s wife could contact the IPK should she require further assistance concerning the welfare of her child and family.
Mohamad Nur Hafiz and two other officers, Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, 40, and Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee, 26, died at about 5.50 pm last Thursday after they were believed to have suffered electric shocks while moving a metal pole outside the Weston Police Station near Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Weston, Beaufort, Sabah. — Bernama

Title: Worried govt producing GMO rice? Agriculture Ministry says Perak run is only a controlled test
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 12 — The proposed genetically modified rice field trial in Perak involving the MR219 variety is only a controlled test plot and does not constitute approval for the use of genetically modified organism (GMO) crops in Malaysia, said Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM) secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
He said the trial was intended to generate scientific evidence and data on GMO, particularly its potential role in addressing food security challenges, rather than to allow its commercial use.
“So we are not allowing GMO to be used, but we need to understand how GMO can perhaps in the future provide for food security.
“If we don’t do this (test), then we don’t know. So that is why there’s a test plot. It’s not an official plot,” he said during a press conference on the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 here today.
He was responding to concerns raised by a group of organisations who had called on the government to reject the proposed field trial involving MR219 in Kampung Kepayang, Perak, citing concerns over food safety, environmental contamination and increased herbicide use.
Isham assured that the test plot would be conducted under controlled, monitored and documented conditions to ensure that any potential issues would not spread beyond the trial area.
“So test plot is something that is controlled, is monitored, recorded, so that it doesn’t… if there’s any issues with the plot, then it doesn’t spread over,” he said.
He said exploring ways to increase productivity was vital to Malaysia’s food security strategy, as the nation continues to grapple with the challenge of maintaining sufficient agricultural land while meeting the food needs of a growing population.
“So currently there’s a lot of pressure in terms of land use. So there is the pressure for land development for housing, for business, for industrial. And there’s also pressure for us to maintain our land acreage to ensure the sustainability and also food security for a long period of time.
“Agriculture use land is slowly being taken over by development, but we need to make sure we can still maintain feeding 34 million people.... with the current land acreage, can they (available land) fulfil that mandate?,” he questioned. — Bernama

Title: Property crime pushes Pahang crime index higher in first seven months of 2026
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 12 — The Pahang crime index increased by 105 cases to 1,262 cases from January to July this year, compared to 1,157 cases for the same period last year.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the rate of resolving crime cases decreased to 59.58 per cent from 71.74 per cent.
“The increase (in crime index) was mainly driven by the rise in property crime cases, which increased to 1,023 cases, compared to 914 cases during the same period last year,” he said when speaking at the Pahang police contingent headquarters (IPK) monthly assembly here today.
He said the Pahang Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (JSJN) recorded 8,277 arrests in the first seven months of this year, compared to 8,243 arrests last year whereas the value of drug seizures decreased significantly to RM8.95 million, compared to RM25.8 million in the same period.
Meanwhile, he said the Pahang Commercial Crime Investigation Department (JSJK) opened 1,893 investigation papers from January to July this year, compared to 1,658 in the same period in 2025.
“A total of 1,380 arrests were made compared to 1,167 arrests last year, while the number of charge sheets increased to 769 from 633,” he said.
Azry Akmar said that although the number of commercial cases increased, the recorded loss value decreased 9.8 per cent to RM46.3 million, compared to RM51.3 million last year.
In an effort to assist scam victims, he said the Pahang JSJK via the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) had seized RM355,355.15, with RM134,546.70 or 37.9 per cent of that amount being returned to the victims.
In terms of traffic aspects, he said the number of road accidents increased to 14,640 cases compared to 14,016 cases last year but the number of fatal accidents decreased to 242 cases compared to 265 cases in the same period.
He added that a total of 129,451 summonses for various traffic offences were issued by the Pahang Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT), with a total compound collection of RM4.94 million. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Govt raises RM48m in sponsorships for Merdeka, Malaysia Day celebrations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 12 — Sponsorships for this year’s Merdeka and Malaysia Day celebrations have risen to more than RM48 million, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced today, describing the contributions as a “public-private partnership” success.
Of the total, RM2.7 million was contributed in cash, while the remaining RM45.93 million comprised contributions in the form of goods and services.
“The ministry is deeply honoured to announce that the total value of sponsorship for HKHM 2026, as verified by the Ministry of Communications Sponsorship Committee to date, amounts to RM48.63 million,” the minister said at an event to celebrate the sponsors here.
“This amount represents a highly encouraging increase of more than 118 per cent compared to last year, which was RM22.3 million.”
Malaysia celebrates its independence on August 31 and Malaysia Day on September 16.
This year’s Merdeka celebration will be held at the iconic Dataran Merdeka.
To date, 139 strategic partners had agreed to contribute to the celebrations. From the total sponsorship value, half is in the form of promotion and 30 percent in the form of goods to be given to visitors.
The remaining 20 per cent consists of sponsorship or the committees involved in organising the two celebrations.
Fahmi asserted the huge participation from mostly the private sector reflected their trust, confidence, and readiness “to come together and make this deeply meaningful celebration a success.”
“Therefore, on behalf of the Ministry of Communications, I express my highest appreciation and heartfelt thanks to all Strategic Partners of HKHM 2026, regardless of the size or value of their contributions,” he said.
Companies that contributed will get tax incentives in return.
Fahmi said the Ministry of Finance has once again approved the celebrations “as a national interest project” pursuant to the provisions under subsection 44(11C) of the Income Tax Act 1967.
This means that, in addition to tax relief for cash contributions, individuals and companies that contribute in-kind from April 1, 2026, to September 16, 2026, can claim a tax deduction of up to 10 percent of their aggregate income for the current assessment year, subject to a ceiling limit of RM15 million.
“Given that the value of in-kind sponsorships this year is highly encouraging and has increased manifold, the Ministry of Communications will submit an appeal to the Ministry of Finance to consider raising the tax deduction incentive ceiling limit for sponsors, God willing,”  the minister said.

Title: Perak DAP says it will remain in unity govt, back Anwar’s reform agenda
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — Perak DAP has unanimously decided to remain in the Unity Government and mobilise the party’s entire machinery to fulfil the people’s mandate and continue the country’s reform agenda.
In a statement today, Perak DAP said the decision was made to deliver on its election promises under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to the statement, Anwar’s leadership had proven successful in implementing various reforms over the past three years, while also enhancing the country’s image and standing on the world stage.
“DAP must continue to demonstrate its capabilities through achievements and work performance so as not to disappoint the people’s expectations.
“By remaining in the government, we can continue implementing the Pakatan Harapan manifesto, including institutional reforms, judicial independence, efforts to combat corruption, reducing the cost of living, reforming the national revenue system, and safeguarding the rights and freedoms of Malaysia’s multiracial society,” the statement said.
Perak DAP stressed the need to fully realise the policies during the current term in order to drive reforms and spur national development for the people’s well-being despite facing various challenges.
The party also remains committed to mobilising all its strength to fulfil the people’s mandate while staying true to the aspirations of the “Malaysia for Malaysians” struggle and remaining mindful of its responsibility to that cause.
The statement also stressed that, in order to safeguard the political strength of an inclusive and progressive multiracial society, DAP needs to remain in the Unity Government to provide a balance and prevent extremist forces from continuing to gain ground.
“Malaysia has witnessed four changes of prime minister over the past seven years. Political instability has affected the economy and investor confidence. That bitter experience must not be repeated, and therefore DAP must not disappoint the mandate given by the people.
“The party must shoulder the responsibility of remaining in the Unity Government until the end of the term to maintain political stability, implement reforms, demonstrate achievements and regain the people’s confidence. This is the right and responsible path,” the statement said.
The position was expressed ahead of the 2026 DAP Party Conference this Sunday, which will determine whether the party remains in or leaves the federal government for the remainder of the current parliamentary term. A motion on the matter will be tabled by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.
The motion will be decided through a vote involving 4,264 delegates from 1,704 eligible branches attending the conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre. — Bernama

Title: Ipoh married couple charged with trafficking 480.6g MDMA, face death penalty
Article:
IPOH, Aug 12 — A married couple was charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 480.6 grammes of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) last week.
Teoh Wai Loon, 44, and Lim Suk Pei, 38, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate S. Punitha, but no plea was recorded as the case falls under the High Court jurisdiction.
According to the charge, they were jointly accused of trafficking 480.6 grammes of MDMA at Room M333, The Pearl Orient Sdn Bhd, Bercham Bistari 4, Medan Bercham Bistari, in the Kinta district, at about 10.30 pm on Aug 4.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, and punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, which provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of not less than 12 strokes if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Zulqarnain Wan Asmira, while both accused were unrepresented.
The court set Dec 7 for case mention to obtain the chemical analysis report.
On Aug 6, police arrested seven individuals, including the couple, for allegedly being involved in a drug trafficking syndicate that had been active since June, following four raids in Ipoh and Tapah.
During the raids, police seized ketamine and MDMA, including about 2.6 kilogrammes of MDMA found at two houses in Tapah.
The drugs seized were estimated to be worth RM538,451, in addition to three vehicles worth RM224,000 and RM32,376 in cash. — Bernama
